/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8026:- **What it does**: Startup resolves a vault path, creates `memory/facts`, `brain`, and `atlas`, builds one in-memory index, wraps it in `vault.Vault`, then exposes a minimal stdio JSON-RPC MCP server with 11 retained memory tools.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8027:- **Why it matters for us**: This is much simpler than our current retrieval runtime and is a useful reference for a lightweight local-first deployment mode, but it is not comparable to our full retrieval stack feature-for-feature.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8028:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8029:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8031:### Finding 2: The main search architecture is “scan markdown -> build in-memory services -> serve from RAM”
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8033:- **What it does**: `Build()` scans all `.md` files, materializes `document` structs, builds a BM25 inverted index, a 256-entry exact-plus-Jaccard query cache, a cross-reference index, and an in-memory fact store; `Search()` then runs cache -> BM25 -> OOD filter -> snippet extraction -> normalized ranking -> cache write.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8034:- **Why it matters for us**: The architecture is operationally cheap and easy to reason about, but it trades away persistent index structures and richer multi-stage fusion for startup-time rebuild simplicity.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8035:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8036:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8038:### Finding 3: Modus splits “all documents” from “memory facts” and gives facts their own recall-and-decay loop
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8040:- **What it does**: Persisted markdown fact files are decayed and reinforced through `vault/facts.go`, while `index/facts.go` keeps a separate in-memory searchable fact slice with recency and confidence boosts; `memory_search` auto-reinforces each returned fact asynchronously, unlike our Stage 2 FSRS testing effect which only writes back when `trackAccess=true`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8041:- **Why it matters for us**: Modus has a cleaner “returned result == recall event” model for fact memories, while our current system is more conservative and avoids write-on-read side effects by default.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8042:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8043:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8045:### Finding 4: Cross-referencing is intentionally shallow adjacency, not a real graph engine
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8047:- **What it does**: Modus builds three adjacency maps (`bySubject`, `byTag`, `byEntity`), scores connected docs with fixed weights (subject `3.0`, entity `2.0`, tag `1.0`), and appends connected-doc hints to search responses. The “second pass” only checks title and subject for entity mentions even though the comments imply broader body linkage.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8048:- **Why it matters for us**: This is weaker than our causal/code-graph style signal layers, but it is much easier to expose to users as understandable “connected docs” rather than invisible score boosts.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8049:- **Recommendation**: adopt now
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8050:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8052:### Finding 5: The markdown layer is very portable, but intentionally loose and only lightly normalized
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8054:- **What it does**: Documents are plain markdown with YAML frontmatter; parse failures fall back to raw body, `ScanDir()` silently skips unreadable/unparseable files and `discard/`, wiki links are extracted from body text, and writes are just frontmatter-plus-body file rewrites after path traversal checks.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8055:- **Why it matters for us**: This is excellent for human editability and git portability, but it also means weaker schema enforcement, silent parse skips, and nondeterministic frontmatter ordering from Go map iteration.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8056:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8057:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8059:### Finding 6: The Librarian is not just documentation rhetoric; it is a real local model dependency in the search architecture
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8061:- **What it does**: When available, the Librarian is contacted over HTTP at `127.0.0.1:8090` and is used for query expansion, result ranking, summarization, fact extraction, intent classification, and briefing production.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8062:- **Why it matters for us**: Modus’s architecture is not purely “BM25 only” in practice once the Librarian is up, so any adoption decision has to treat LLM-mediated lexical expansion as an optional subsystem with availability and correctness risks.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8063:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8064:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8066:### Finding 7: Public already has the broader retrieval architecture; Modus is a simplification reference, not a replacement candidate
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8068:- **What it does**: Public already runs a 4-stage hybrid pipeline with vector + BM25/FTS5 + graph channels, session and causal boosts, reranking, fallback-state reporting, and opt-in FSRS write-back. Modus is simpler, but the README also overstates some properties: `go.mod` is not zero-dependency, and the search path can invoke a local model when Librarian is available.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8069:- **Why it matters for us**: The real comparison is selective borrowing, not replacement. The highest-value overlaps are adjacency hints and a cleaner recall-event policy; the rest would mostly duplicate or downgrade existing Public capabilities.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8070:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8071:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8073:## Sources Consulted
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8095:## Assessment
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8101:## Reflection
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8106:## Recommended Next Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8111:# Iteration 002: CORE DATA MODEL
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8113:## Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8116:## Findings
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8118:### Finding 1: Modus has no durable search index; it rebuilds the entire retrieval model from markdown on startup
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8120:- **What it does**: `Index` is just RAM state: `docs`, `bm25Engine`, `queryCache`, `factStore`, `crossIndex`, and a `meta` map keyed by path. `Build()` rescans markdown, projects it into `document` structs, then rebuilds BM25 postings, cross refs, and in-memory fact indexes; `Open()` ignores the supplied `indexPath` and simply rebuilds from `~/modus/vault` or `MODUS_VAULT_DIR`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8121:- **Why it matters for us**: This is simpler than our SQLite-backed model, but it means no persistent index state, no schema migration layer for retrieval data, and no incremental durability for derived structures. For Public, this would be a storage downgrade, not a simplification win.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8122:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8123:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8125:### Finding 2: The authoritative schema is loose YAML frontmatter plus body; indexed structs are only lossy projections
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8127:- **What it does**: `Document` stores `Frontmatter map[string]interface{}` and `Body`; getters are lightweight (`GetFloat` only handles numeric YAML types, not strings), and writes just serialize the map back out. Searchable `document` structs flatten only selected fields (`Path`, `Source`, `Subject`, `Title`, `Tags`, `Body`, `Predicate`, `Confidence`, `Importance`, `Kind`, `Created`, `Triage`) while keeping the raw map on the side.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8128:- **Why it matters for us**: This is excellent for human-editable, git-friendly storage, but schema discipline is mostly conventional, not enforced. The most plausible use for Public is as an interchange/export layer, not as a replacement for typed persistent storage.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8129:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8130:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8132:### Finding 3: Modus has an immediate consistency split between file writes and searchable state
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8134:- **What it does**: `vault_write`, `memory_store`, and `ReinforceFact` mutate markdown files directly. But `vault_search`, `vault_connected`, and `memory_search` only read the prebuilt in-memory `Index`, `factStore`, and `crossIndex`. Meanwhile `vault_list` and `memory_facts` rescan disk live, so they can see writes the search path cannot.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8135:- **Why it matters for us**: This is a real storage-model weakness, not just a UX wrinkle: the system is not read-your-write consistent across tools. A newly stored fact can be listable but not searchable, and reinforced files can persist updated FSRS metadata while search still uses stale RAM copies. Public’s persisted DB plus consumer rebind path is materially safer.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8136:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8137:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8139:### Finding 4: FSRS state is persisted directly in markdown fact files, but the active fact-search model ignores most of it
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8141:- **What it does**: `DecayFacts()` and `ReinforceFact()` write `confidence`, `stability`, `difficulty`, `last_accessed`, `access_count`, `last_decayed`, and archival flags into fact frontmatter. But `MemFact` only materializes a smaller subset, and `factStore.search()` ranks on term overlap, a small confidence bonus, and created-date recency; it does not use stored stability, difficulty, or access history.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8142:- **Why it matters for us**: Modus’s files carry cognitively meaningful state, but its query-time model only partially consumes that state. The useful lesson for Public is not to copy the thinner fact model, but to consider exposing our own persisted FSRS state more transparently when that helps operators reason about memory freshness.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8143:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8144:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8146:### Finding 5: Identity is path-derived, not stable, so renames are semantic changes
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8148:- **What it does**: Search hits and facts are identified by relative path; `MemFact.ID` is the relative markdown path, dedup uses `Path`, and `memory_reinforce` takes a path. New facts are slugged from `subject-predicate` and collision-suffixed. There is no Modus-side equivalent of Public’s `memory_lineage` + `active_memory_projection` stable logical identity model.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8149:- **Why it matters for us**: This is fine for a small personal vault, but path-based identity makes renames and moves double as identity changes, which weakens continuity for reinforcement history, links, and long-lived references. Public’s lineage tables are substantially stronger for evolving memories.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8150:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8151:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8153:### Finding 6: Public already has the richer persisted storage graph; Modus is a portability reference, not a schema upgrade
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8155:- **What it does**: Public persists a unified `memory_index` row with provenance, governance scope, FSRS fields, chunking, quality, and `content_text`, then derives `memory_fts`, `vec_memories`, `causal_edges`, `memory_summaries`, `memory_entities`, `entity_catalog`, `memory_lineage`, and `active_memory_projection`. DB consumers can rebind when the backing SQLite handle changes, and FSRS strengthening on retrieval is opt-in via `trackAccess`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8156:- **Why it matters for us**: The storage-layer gap is architectural, not incremental. Modus’s value is in transparent file-native ergonomics and understandable portability, but its underlying persistence model is much weaker than what Public already has.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8157:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8158:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8160:## Sources Consulted
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8185:## Assessment
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8190:## Reflection
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8194:## Recommended Next Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8207:# Iteration 003: TOOL/API SURFACE
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8209:## Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8212:## Findings
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8214:### Finding 1: Modus exposes a very thin MCP transport: stdio JSON-RPC with only `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8216:- **What it does**: `Server.Run()` reads newline-delimited JSON from stdin and `handle()` only recognizes `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`. The binary starts this server directly from `main.go` after building the in-memory index and registering tools. There is no inbound HTTP listener, no resource/prompt surface, no session bootstrap tool, and no orchestration layer comparable to Public’s `memory_context`, `session_bootstrap`, `code_graph_query`, or `code_graph_context`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8217:- **Why it matters for us**: This is a portability win for a single-purpose local binary, but it is a surface-area downgrade relative to Public’s retrieval/orchestration server. It is useful as a minimal transport reference, not as a model for Public’s primary MCP surface.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8218:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8219:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8221:### Finding 2: Modus has hidden profile separation in code, but the shipped binary hard-wires a single 11-tool profile
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8223:- **What it does**: `RegisterVaultTools()` defines a much larger tool family (`atlas_*`, `qm_*`, `distill_status`, plus memory/vault tools). `RegisterMemoryTools()` first calls `RegisterVaultTools()` and then destructively deletes every tool not in its 11-tool allowlist. `RegisterLearningsTools()` defines a separate `modus_learnings_*` family, but `main.go` never wires it. Separately, `docs/librarian.md` recommends a 6-tool “librarian” subset in agent config, but that subset is documentation-only, not a negotiated runtime profile.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8224:- **Why it matters for us**: The codebase clearly wants multiple role-specific surfaces, but the implementation is manual, non-discoverable, and not caller-selectable. Public could benefit from explicit tool-profile projections, but Modus’s current approach is too brittle to copy directly.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8225:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8226:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8228:### Finding 3: The only real API endpoints are outbound sidecar calls to the local Librarian model, not Modus-owned service endpoints
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8230:- **What it does**: Modus hard-codes `http://127.0.0.1:8090` as the Librarian endpoint, probes `/health` with `/v1/models` fallback, and posts chat requests to `/v1/chat/completions`. `ExpandQuery()`, `RankResults()`, `ExtractFacts()`, `ClassifyIntent()`, and `ProduceBriefing()` all run through this local OpenAI-compatible sidecar, but none are exposed as MCP tools themselves. MCP callers only see higher-level tools whose behavior changes if `librarian.Available()` returns true.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8231:- **Why it matters for us**: The useful pattern is “optional local lexical-expansion/rerank sidecar,” not the hard-coded localhost contract. Public could prototype an internal expander/reranker channel, but should keep it capability-checked, configurable, and traceable rather than ambient and endpoint-bound.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8232:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8233:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8235:### Finding 4: Tool registration and argument validation are loose enough that adopting Modus’s MCP schema pattern would weaken Public
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8237:- **What it does**: Modus stores `InputSchema` as generic `interface{}` and passes raw `map[string]interface{}` into handlers. Validation is decentralized and uneven: many handlers use loose type assertions and defaults, while filesystem safety is enforced mostly by `vault.safePath()` on read/write/list operations. Public, by contrast, has centralized schema definitions, strict Zod validation, explicit `additionalProperties: false`, safe path validators, and governance/session fields baked into tool schemas.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8238:- **Why it matters for us**: This is a material safety and operability gap. Public’s current tool layer is already stronger on input validation, scope governance, and explicit contracts; replacing it with Modus’s pattern would be regression, not simplification.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8239:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8240:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8242:### Finding 5: Modus search tools hide side effects and capability changes behind ambient conditions rather than explicit flags
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8244:- **What it does**: `vault_search` silently switches to librarian-expanded multi-query retrieval when the sidecar is reachable, otherwise falls back to direct search. `memory_search` silently spawns async `ReinforceFact()` calls for every returned fact. There are no per-call controls for disabling reinforcement, forcing plain lexical search, asking for provenance, selecting a presentation profile, or scoping session behavior. Public exposes those controls explicitly through `trackAccess`, `includeTrace`, `profile`, `sessionId`, intent routing, and governed scope fields.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8245:- **Why it matters for us**: Search-as-read with hidden write side effects is risky for operators and harder to reason about in evaluations. Public’s explicit opt-in `trackAccess` model is materially safer and easier to benchmark than Modus’s always-on recall reinforcement.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8246:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8247:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8249:### Finding 6: Modus’s CLI is a real second operator surface, separate from MCP, and that split is one of the cleaner parts of the design
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8251:- **What it does**: The binary has a tiny command surface: `version`, `health`, `doctor`, and `import khoj`, with `--vault` or `MODUS_VAULT_DIR` selecting the vault. `doctor` performs structural diagnostics over markdown files and `import khoj` handles migration into vault folders. This is separate from the MCP tool plane and clearly aimed at human operators or one-shot maintenance tasks.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8252:- **Why it matters for us**: Public already has rich MCP health/status/index tools, but a thin human-facing CLI wrapper for common operator flows—health, validate, reindex, diagnose—could improve ergonomics for local maintenance and CI without changing core retrieval architecture.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8253:- **Recommendation**: NEW FEATURE
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8254:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8256:## Sources Consulted
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8281:## Assessment
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8286:## Reflection
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8290:## Recommended Next Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8304:# Iteration 004: SESSION LIFECYCLE
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8306:## Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8309:## Findings
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8311:### Finding 1: Modus has no first-class session object; a “session” is just process startup plus a disk-backed vault snapshot
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8313:- **What it does**: `main.go` resolves the vault path, creates a few directories, rebuilds the in-memory index, registers tools, and enters the stdio MCP loop. `server.go` only handles `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`; it does not mint session IDs, persist client state, or expose resume/bootstrap/close semantics. By contrast, Public’s `memory_context` resolves trusted server-managed sessions and persists lifecycle state through `session-manager.ts`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8314:- **Why it matters for us**: Modus’s cross-chat continuity comes from durable files, not session lifecycle management. That is simpler, but it is not a substitute for Public’s explicit session continuity surface (`memory_context`, `session_resume`, `session_bootstrap`, trusted `sessionId`, saved state).
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8315:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8316:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8318:### Finding 2: Live-session maintenance is snapshot-based, so Modus does not really “learn during the current session” without restart
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8320:- **What it does**: `index.Build()` creates an in-memory `Index` and fact store once at startup. During a session, `memory_search` asynchronously calls `ReinforceFact`, while `StoreFact`, `DecayFacts`, `ArchiveStaleFacts`, and `TouchFact` all mutate markdown on disk. But subsequent search still reads the old in-memory snapshot because there is no hot reload, invalidation, or rebuild in the running process.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8321:- **Why it matters for us**: For session lifecycle, this means Modus’s memory state does not evolve coherently inside a live conversation. Public’s model is materially stronger because it treats session continuity and retrieval state as active managed state, not just files that will matter after restart.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8322:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8323:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8325:### Finding 3: The only session-like metadata is mostly non-operative, and one of its freshness signals is broken
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8327:- **What it does**: Modus projects `session_tag` into `MemFact.SessionTag`, but only while indexing; if missing, `indexer.go` defaults it to `"session-1"`. `StoreFact()` does not write a `session_tag`, and no MCP tool exposes session-scoped filtering or retrieval. Separately, `StoreFact()` writes `created: "now"`, while `recencyBoost()` and `Tier()` expect ISO/date strings, so newly stored facts can miss “hot/warm” treatment and fall back to neutral/cold handling.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8328:- **Why it matters for us**: This is not enough structure to support session creation, session-local recall, or accurate “recent conversation” prioritization. Public already has explicit lifecycle metadata like trusted `sessionId`, `effectiveSessionId`, `resumed`, event counters, `contextSummary`, and `pendingWork`; Modus’s passive metadata is too weak to borrow directly.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8329:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8330:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8332:### Finding 4: Modus has summarization helpers, but no actual end-of-session or resume-summary pipeline wires them in
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8334:- **What it does**: `SummarizeForCloud()` can compress search hits, and `ProduceBriefing()` can generate a five-bucket briefing from ingested items plus active missions. But there are no call sites for either helper in the shipped runtime, and `server.go` simply exits on EOF without any session-finalization hook. Public, by contrast, has cached continuity summaries in `session-resume.ts`, a one-call recovery tool in `session-bootstrap.ts`, and checkpoint generation in `session-manager.ts`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8335:- **Why it matters for us**: The useful idea is not Modus’s current lifecycle, because there effectively isn’t one. The transferable part is the **shape** of `ProduceBriefing()` as a structured end-of-cycle summary format that Public could test as an alternate session-summary profile.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8336:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8337:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8339:### Finding 5: Modus’s strongest “context survival across sessions” idea is the learnings subsystem, but it is dormant in the shipped binary
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8341:- **What it does**: The learnings subsystem is explicitly designed to persist “console-level” operational lessons across model swaps and format them for prompt injection via `LoadForPrompt()`. But `main.go` never calls `RegisterLearningsTools()`, so none of that cross-model continuity is available from the runtime that users actually launch.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8342:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the clearest Modus-side attempt at continuity beyond raw fact recall: a separate, reusable memory plane for durable operator guidance. Public could consider a similarly explicit “operational learnings” channel, but only if it is truly first-class and not hidden behind unwired code.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8343:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8344:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8346:### Finding 6: Multi-client continuity in Modus is shared-file persistence, not isolated session continuity
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8348:- **What it does**: The README says each AI client starts its own Modus process against the same vault, with index rebuild on startup and “last writer wins” at the file level for concurrent writes. That matches the code architecture: no shared session registry, no per-client isolation, and no recovery contract beyond reopening the vault and rebuilding the snapshot.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8349:- **Why it matters for us**: This is fine for lightweight portability, but it is a poor fit for Public’s richer session semantics, where separate sessions can be trusted, resumed, checkpointed, completed, interrupted, and garbage-collected explicitly.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8350:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8351:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8353:## Sources Consulted
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8373:## Assessment
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8378:## Reflection
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8382:## Recommended Next Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8395:# Iteration 005: SEARCH MECHANISMS
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8397:## Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8400:## Findings
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8402:### Finding 1: Modus is **not** a vector or true hybrid retriever; it is a BM25-only engine with optional LLM query rewrites
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8404:- **What it does**: Modus builds one in-memory lexical index over six fields with fixed weights `{path 1.5, source 1.0, subject 2.0, title 3.0, tags 1.5, body 1.0}`, tokenizes/stems locally, and falls back to prefix matching for terms of length `>=3`. The only “hybrid” element in shipped search is librarian-driven query expansion before rerunning the same lexical engine. There is no vector lane, no learned fusion, and no cross-channel score combination. Public already has explicit hybrid retrieval: weighted FTS5 BM25, embedding/vector retrieval, multi-variant deep mode, and RRF-based fusion.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8405:- **Why it matters for us**: Modus is useful as a compact lexical baseline, but it is not evidence for replacing Public’s hybrid stack. Its field-weight idea is already overlapped here, and our current lexical weights are actually stronger and more structured.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8406:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8407:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8409:### Finding 2: Modus expands queries, but merges variant results with **first-seen dedup**, not global re-ranking
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8411:- **What it does**: `ExpandQuery()` always keeps the original query first, appends up to five additional strings, and `vault_search` / `memory_search` then append results variant-by-variant while deduplicating by `path` or `subject|predicate`. After dedup, Modus simply truncates to `limit`; it does not merge scores across branches or globally re-rank the union. A librarian `RankResults()` helper exists, but the only call site is its own definition. Public, by contrast, preserves branch/source provenance per candidate and fuses later in the pipeline.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8412:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the biggest ranking weakness in Modus’s “hybrid-like” behavior. Expansion can improve recall, but Modus’s merge policy means later variants often cannot beat early lexical hits even if they are more relevant.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8413:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8414:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8416:### Finding 3: The cache idea is useful, but the shipped Jaccard/LRU implementation is unsafe and only partially correct
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8418:- **What it does**: Modus adds a two-tier cache: exact query hash match first, then fuzzy reuse when token-set Jaccard similarity is `>=0.6`, with `256` max entries. That part is interesting. But `get()` mutates `hits` while holding only `RLock`, and cache reads never increment the global counter, so its “LRU” recency signal is not actually advanced on access.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8419:- **Why it matters for us**: The architectural idea is stronger than the implementation. Public already has exact-argument caching around `memory_search`; a safe lexical/paraphrase cache could still be worth exploring for repeated nearby queries, but Modus’s version should not be copied.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8420:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8421:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8423:### Finding 4: README latency claims only fit the pure in-memory BM25 path; the default librarian-expanded path can be network/LLM-bound
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8425:- **What it does**: Modus advertises `<100µs` cached search and `<5ms` cold search, which is believable for the in-memory BM25/cache path after startup. But when the librarian is reachable, both `vault_search` and `memory_search` first do a health probe and then send a chat-completions request with a `120s` HTTP timeout to generate expansions. That makes the real default search path dependent on external model latency, not just BM25 speed. Public’s deep expansion path is explicitly gated and wrapped in a `5s` timeout budget.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8426:- **Why it matters for us**: The Modus performance story is valid only for one branch of the runtime. We should not import its “always expand when available” behavior into Public’s main retrieval path.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8427:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8428:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8430:### Finding 5: Modus’s fact lane is **not BM25**, and it couples search with automatic write-side reinforcement
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8432:- **What it does**: `memory_search` prints `bm25+librarian`, but the fact lane uses a separate `factStore.search()` that scores by token overlap, a small inverse-hit-frequency heuristic, `confidence * 0.1`, and a coarse recency multiplier. It is not BM25. Then every returned fact is asynchronously reinforced via `go v.ReinforceFact(...)`, so read access mutates stored state by default. Public already has FSRS strengthening logic, but only behind explicit `trackAccess=true`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8433:- **Why it matters for us**: Modus’s fact path is closer to a lightweight subject/value recall lane than a full lexical ranker. The automatic reinforcement loop is also too write-happy for Public’s default search semantics.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8434:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8435:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8437:### Finding 6: Cross-reference hints are the best transferable search-side idea, but only as a lightweight appendix, not as a ranking core
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8439:- **What it does**: Modus builds adjacency maps keyed by normalized subject, tag, and entity name, then scores connected docs with fixed weights `subject=3`, `entity=2`, `tag=1`. This is cheap and useful for related-document surfacing. But it is intentionally shallow: no traversal, no causal semantics, and the “scan title/body for entity mentions” comment only checks title and subject in code. Public already has richer graph-aware ranking signals, causal boost, and structural freshness augmentation.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8440:- **Why it matters for us**: The transferable piece is presentation, not retrieval replacement. Modus shows a cheap way to append “related memory” hints beside primary search hits without requiring full graph traversal on every query.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8441:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8442:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8444:## Sources Consulted
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8466:## Assessment
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8471:## Reflection
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8475:## Recommended Next Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8488:# Iteration 006: MEMORY HYGIENE
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8490:## Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8493:## Findings
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8495:### Finding 1: Modus has no true fact upsert; it appends filename variants and hides duplicates at read time
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8497:- **What it does**: `StoreFact()` derives a slug from `subject + "-" + predicate`, then resolves collisions by creating `-2`, `-3`, etc. files instead of updating an existing logical fact. Those duplicates are all indexed into the in-memory fact store. `memory_search` later deduplicates only at response time via `subject|predicate`, so duplication is masked rather than prevented.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8498:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the opposite of hygienic memory mutation. It accumulates duplicate fact files and lets retrieval paper over the problem. Public already has same-path/content-hash dedup plus append-only supersede behavior when content actually changes, so Modus’s write pattern would be a regression.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8499:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8500:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8502:### Finding 2: Modus mutations do not refresh the live in-memory fact store, so hygiene is stale until restart
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8504:- **What it does**: Modus builds its index once at startup. `memory_store`, `memory_reinforce`, `memory_decay_facts`, and `memory_archive_stale` all rewrite markdown files, but none update `idx.facts` or rebuild the index. Even automatic reinforcement from `memory_search` is just `go v.ReinforceFact(f.ID)`, so the persisted file changes asynchronously while the live search store stays unchanged.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8505:- **Why it matters for us**: This is a major runtime hygiene flaw: dedup state, confidence, archive flags, and freshness are not read-your-writes consistent. Public’s mutation path updates DB state, BM25 state, lineage, and cache invalidation immediately; Modus does not.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8506:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8507:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8509:### Finding 3: Modus archive is only a partial soft-delete and its visibility rules are inconsistent
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8511:- **What it does**: `ArchiveStaleFacts()` sets `archived=true` and `archived_at`, but `ListFacts()` does not filter archived files, so `memory_facts` still lists them. Only the startup-time fact index marks archived facts inactive for search. The memory tool surface exposes archive, decay, reinforce, and store, but no per-fact delete/update/restore workflow.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8512:- **Why it matters for us**: Modus’s “soft delete” is not a coherent lifecycle state; it is a flag with inconsistent read behavior and no garbage-collection story beyond accumulation on disk. Public already distinguishes archived visibility at query time and offers explicit delete/checkpoint workflows.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8513:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8514:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8516:### Finding 4: Topic-key stability is weak because Modus uses raw strings, not canonical alias-backed identities
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8518:- **What it does**: Fact lookup keys are just `strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(subject))`; cross-ref keys are lowercased subject/tag/title text; entity resolution tries slug/name matching and finally a substring walk. There is no alias table or canonical subject/topic identifier, so spelling variants fragment neighborhoods.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8519:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the biggest hygiene gap around topic stability. Public already does better on file identity and entity alias normalization, but Modus is a useful warning that exact-string topic keys are brittle. The lesson is worth exploring, but Modus’s implementation is not.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8520:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8521:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8523:### Finding 5: `vault_write` is a destructive overwrite path with no revision trail, checkpoint, or append-only semantics
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8525:- **What it does**: `vault_write` passes arbitrary path/frontmatter/body to `v.Write()`, which directly calls `markdown.Write()`, which directly calls `os.WriteFile()`. That means overwrite-in-place, no revision record, no checkpoint, no mutation ledger, and no logical predecessor/successor relationship.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8526:- **Why it matters for us**: This is a clear memory-hygiene mismatch with Public’s mutation model. Public mutations are transactional and auditable; Modus exposes a generic write primitive that can erase provenance in one call.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8527:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8528:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8530:### Finding 6: Newly stored facts begin with `created: "now"`, which breaks Modus’s own recency and decay heuristics
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8532:- **What it does**: `StoreFact()` writes a literal `created: "now"`. The shared `parseTime()` helper accepts RFC3339/date layouts only, so fresh facts cannot use `created` as a valid decay fallback. `recencyBoost()` and `StalenessWarning()` also fail open when that timestamp is unparseable.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:8533:- **Why it matters for us**: This is a concrete hygiene bug, not just a design tradeoff. A newly stored fact begins life outside the system’s own freshness/decay contract. Public’s save path writes machine-readable timestamps and lineage metadata, so Modus offers nothing to adopt here.
