/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9771:### Finding 1: Explicit graded review is the best immediate transfer
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9773:- **What it does**: Modus exposes `memory_reinforce`, but only as a success-only reinforce action. Public already has the stronger primitive: graded FSRS review (`AGAIN/HARD/GOOD/EASY`) plus computed `nextReviewDate`, yet the exposed adjacent tool is only `memory_validate(wasUseful)`, which adjusts confidence rather than recording a real review event.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9774:- **Why it matters for us**: This closes the clearest control-plane gap without changing retrieval architecture. It also makes any later review queue trustworthy because review history would record hard recalls and lapses, not only “useful / not useful.”
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9775:- **Recommendation**: adopt now
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9776:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9778:### Finding 2: A doctor-style summary should ship beside review
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9780:- **What it does**: Modus’s `doctor` turns vault health into a one-screen operator report. Public already has deeper health and repair machinery—FTS rebuild, orphan cleanup, degraded/healthy state, confirmation-gated repair—but exposes it as a richer technical envelope.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9781:- **Why it matters for us**: This is mostly presentation work, not backend work. It improves operator trust immediately while preserving Public’s stronger repair semantics underneath.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9782:- **Recommendation**: adopt now
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9783:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9785:### Finding 3: Keep one retrieval core; Modus’s split fact-search paths are a warning
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9787:- **What it does**: Modus has multiple fact-search contracts for the same memory objects: `Index.SearchFacts`, a separate in-memory `factStore`, and `Vault.SearchFacts` fallback behavior. Public routes `memory_search` through one pipeline contract via `executePipeline`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9788:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the strongest architectural lesson from Modus’s weaknesses. Public should keep specialized search surfaces as thin wrappers over the canonical pipeline instead of growing parallel ranking rules that will drift.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9789:- **Recommendation**: adopt now
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9790:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9792:### Finding 4: `memory_due` is real product value, but it needs an authoritative due-state contract first
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9794:- **What it does**: Modus visibly ties search recall, reinforce, decay, and archive to one fact state. Public already stores `stability`, `difficulty`, `last_review`, `review_count`, and opt-in access effects, and computes `nextReviewDate`, but does not expose an operator-facing due queue.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9795:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the biggest missing workflow surface in Public. But it should not ship until “due” is defined as either persisted state (`next_review_at`) or a deterministic derivation from existing FSRS fields.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9796:- **Recommendation**: NEW FEATURE
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9797:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9799:### Finding 5: Durable proposal inboxes are the best non-retrieval idea Modus has
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9801:- **What it does**: Modus persists risky knowledge changes as markdown PR artifacts, then merge/reject outcomes reinforce or weaken linked beliefs. Public already produces advisory reconsolidation recommendations and confidence feedback, but the recommendation is transient and not stored as a durable review object.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9802:- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s next gap is operator workflow, not mutation safety. A persistent inbox for reconsolidation, supersession, promotion, and deprecation proposals would let existing confidence and mutation systems work as a real review loop.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9803:- **Recommendation**: NEW FEATURE
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9804:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9806:### Finding 6: Connected-doc hints are worth prototyping only as an explanation appendix
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9808:- **What it does**: Modus builds lightweight subject/entity/tag adjacency and appends connected docs that did not make the main ranked list. The weighting is simple and fixed (`subject 3`, `entity 2`, `tag 1`).
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9809:- **Why it matters for us**: The transferable part is explanation, not ranking. Public can test a “related memories” appendix without diluting stronger graph-backed or hybrid scoring paths.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9810:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9811:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9813:### Finding 7: Lexical-only expansion belongs only in weak-result recovery
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9815:- **What it does**: Modus asks the Librarian for 3-5 keyword variants, searches each, deduplicates, and caps results. It is lightweight, but ungrounded and union-first.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9816:- **Why it matters for us**: Public already has a more complex retrieval pipeline, so copying this as a mainline branch would mostly add noise and latency. The only credible transfer is a tightly bounded fallback when hybrid retrieval is weak.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9817:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9818:- **Impact**: low
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9820:### Finding 8: Content-level contradiction and duplicate-fact linting is still worth a prototype
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9822:- **What it does**: Modus’s `doctor` explicitly flags missing `subject`/`predicate`, duplicate `subject+predicate` pairs, and contradictory values for the same pair. Public’s current health surface is stronger on infrastructure integrity than on fact-content linting.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9823:- **Why it matters for us**: This complements Public’s existing infra health checks instead of replacing them. It is one of the few Modus hygiene ideas that adds net-new value.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9824:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9825:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9827:### Finding 9: Reject Modus’s fuzzy Jaccard result-cache contract
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9829:- **What it does**: Modus reuses cached result sets on exact hash hits or Jaccard-similar query term sets. Public’s search surface has too many scoring knobs—scope, archived filtering, session/causal boost, rerank, quality thresholds, trace/profile flags—for fuzzy query reuse to be safe.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9830:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the wrong cache contract for Public. Similar text is not enough to guarantee equivalent retrieval intent or scoring context.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9831:- **Recommendation**: reject

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9834:### Finding 10: Reject Modus’s permissive markdown parse/write contract
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9836:- **What it does**: Modus treats malformed YAML as body, skips parse failures during scans, and writes markdown directly with minimal validation. That is good for a personal vault, but it optimizes for permissiveness over authoritative ingestion.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9837:- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s memory layer is intentionally more governed. Regressing to Modus’s permissive storage contract would weaken memory integrity for little gain.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9838:- **Recommendation**: reject

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9843:- **What it does**: Modus treats every returned fact as a successful recall and asynchronously reinforces it. Public already supports access effects, but keeps them explicit with `trackAccess=false` by default.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9844:- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s graded FSRS model is stronger than Modus’s success-only reinforce loop. Default write-on-read would blur retrieval and review, inflate successful-recall history, and make future due-state less trustworthy.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9845:- **Recommendation**: reject

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/003-modus-memory-main/research/research.md:9850:- **What it does**: Modus persists trust stage and exposes get/set tools, but current code does not use that state to gate PR or other mutation tools. It is posture metadata, not enforced runtime policy.

If autonomy stages are added, they must actually gate review, proposal, or mutation flows.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5942:### Finding 1: The external repo is a deliberately thin wrapper, not a full memory engine
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5945:- **What it does**: the whole plugin surface lives in one entrypoint: OpenCode loads the plugin, resolves `ctx.directory || ctx.worktree || process.cwd()`, derives a project key, shells out to `mnemosyne`, registers five tools, and adds one compaction hook. `package.json` publishes only `dist`, and there is no in-repo AGENTS file or deeper architecture layer to inspect.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5946:- **Why it matters for us**: the transfer value is wrapper ergonomics and lifecycle design, not hidden TypeScript retrieval logic. We should treat backend claims as an interface contract, not as code we can adopt line-for-line.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5947:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5948:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5950:### Finding 2: Project/global scoping is the main product decision in the wrapper
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5953:- **What it does**: project scope is derived from the current directory basename, normalized so literal `global` becomes `default`; project collections are auto-initialized on plugin load, while the global collection is lazily initialized only on first `memory_store_global`. The tool surface makes project/global choice explicit with separate recall/store variants.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5954:- **Why it matters for us**: Public already supports scoped retrieval, but not with this lightweight agent-facing split. The ergonomic gain is real, but basename-derived identity risks collisions across similarly named folders, nested worktrees, or renamed repositories.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5955:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5956:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5958:### Finding 3: The CLI bridge is secure-by-construction, but shifts complexity into binary/runtime operations
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5961:- **What it does**: the wrapper uses `Bun.spawn(["mnemosyne", ...args])` with `cwd: targetDir`, reads both stdout and stderr, throws on non-zero exit, and special-cases missing-binary errors into a user-facing install message. That avoids shell interpolation risk, but it also assumes Bun, a separately installed Go binary, and a first-run model download of about 500 MB.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5962:- **Why it matters for us**: this is a clean plugin boundary if we ever want a standalone memory binary, but it trades in-process native-module complexity for external install, model bootstrap, and support burden.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5963:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5964:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5966:### Finding 4: Mnemosyne’s hybrid retrieval story is mostly README contract; Public already implements the deeper live pipeline
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5969:- **What it does**: the wrapper only quotes the user query and forwards it to `mnemosyne search --format plain`; the README alone claims FTS5/BM25 plus sqlite-vec cosine similarity plus Reciprocal Rank Fusion with `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5`. By contrast, Public explicitly documents and implements a hybrid path with `executePipeline`, vector/FTS/BM25 channels, query routing, and RRF fusion.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5970:- **Why it matters for us**: we should reject any conclusion that Mnemosyne introduces hybrid retrieval as a net-new capability for Public. The real novelty is wrapper shape, scoping ergonomics, and compaction guidance.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5971:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5972:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5974:### Finding 5: The compaction hook is the strongest transferable idea because it preserves tool awareness, not just context payload
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5977:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne pushes a static instruction block into `output.context` during `experimental.session.compacting`, explicitly naming `memory_recall`, `memory_store`, `memory_delete`, and the global variants. Public already preserves structural context through the compact-code-graph transport and can prepend surfaced constitutional/triggered memories during compaction, but that path does not add the same blunt “you still have these memory tools, and here is when to use them” reminder.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5978:- **Why it matters for us**: this is a low-cost, high-leverage addition for compaction resilience. Structural continuity and surfaced memories help, but direct tool reminders reduce the chance that the agent forgets to recall/store/delete after a context reset.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:5979:- **Recommendation**: adopt now

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6024:## Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6027:## Findings
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6029:### Finding 1: The external repo is a deliberately thin wrapper, not a full memory engine
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6032:- **What it does**: the whole plugin surface lives in one entrypoint: OpenCode loads the plugin, resolves `ctx.directory || ctx.worktree || process.cwd()`, derives a project key, shells out to `mnemosyne`, registers five tools, and adds one compaction hook. `package.json` publishes only `dist`, and there is no in-repo AGENTS file or deeper architecture layer to inspect.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6033:- **Why it matters for us**: the transfer value is wrapper ergonomics and lifecycle design, not hidden TypeScript retrieval logic. We should treat backend claims as an interface contract, not as code we can adopt line-for-line.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6034:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6035:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6037:### Finding 2: Project/global scoping is the main product decision in the wrapper
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6040:- **What it does**: project scope is derived from the current directory basename, normalized so literal `global` becomes `default`; project collections are auto-initialized on plugin load, while the global collection is lazily initialized only on first `memory_store_global`. The tool surface makes project/global choice explicit with separate recall/store variants.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6041:- **Why it matters for us**: Public already supports scoped retrieval, but not with this lightweight agent-facing split. The ergonomic gain is real, but basename-derived identity risks collisions across similarly named folders, nested worktrees, or renamed repositories.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6042:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6043:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6045:### Finding 3: The CLI bridge is secure-by-construction, but shifts complexity into binary/runtime operations
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6048:- **What it does**: the wrapper uses `Bun.spawn(["mnemosyne", ...args])` with `cwd: targetDir`, reads both stdout and stderr, throws on non-zero exit, and special-cases missing-binary errors into a user-facing install message. That avoids shell interpolation risk, but it also assumes Bun, a separately installed Go binary, and a first-run model download of about 500 MB.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6049:- **Why it matters for us**: this is a clean plugin boundary if we ever want a standalone memory binary, but it trades in-process native-module complexity for external install, model bootstrap, and support burden.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6050:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6051:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6053:### Finding 4: Mnemosyne’s hybrid retrieval story is mostly README contract; Public already implements the deeper live pipeline
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6056:- **What it does**: the wrapper only quotes the user query and forwards it to `mnemosyne search --format plain`; the README alone claims FTS5/BM25 plus sqlite-vec cosine similarity plus Reciprocal Rank Fusion with `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5`. By contrast, Public explicitly documents and implements a hybrid path with `executePipeline`, vector/FTS/BM25 channels, query routing, and RRF fusion.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6057:- **Why it matters for us**: we should reject any conclusion that Mnemosyne introduces hybrid retrieval as a net-new capability for Public. The real novelty is wrapper shape, scoping ergonomics, and compaction guidance.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6058:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6059:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6061:### Finding 5: The compaction hook is the strongest transferable idea because it preserves tool awareness, not just context payload
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6064:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne pushes a static instruction block into `output.context` during `experimental.session.compacting`, explicitly naming `memory_recall`, `memory_store`, `memory_delete`, and the global variants. Public already preserves structural context through the compact-code-graph transport and can prepend surfaced constitutional/triggered memories during compaction, but that path does not add the same blunt “you still have these memory tools, and here is when to use them” reminder.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6065:- **Why it matters for us**: this is a low-cost, high-leverage addition for compaction resilience. Structural continuity and surfaced memories help, but direct tool reminders reduce the chance that the agent forgets to recall/store/delete after a context reset.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6066:- **Recommendation**: adopt now
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6067:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6069:### Finding 6: Mnemosyne’s AGENTS guidance is reusable, but CocoIndex should remain a separate system
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:6072:- **What it does**: the README recommends a concrete operating rhythm: recall at session start, store after meaningful decisions, delete contradicted memories, use global variants for cross-project facts, and reserve core for always-needed context. /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19016:- **What it does**: the plugin only shells out to `mnemosyne init/search/add/delete`; the published package ships only `dist`, and all FTS5/BM25/sqlite-vec/RRF details live in the README rather than in inspectable schema or migration code in this repo.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19017:- **Why it matters for us**: this repo is not a storage-model blueprint. It proves a tool boundary and a backend contract, but not the backend’s actual table layout, migration strategy, or deletion/versioning semantics.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19018:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19020:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19022:### Finding 2: Mnemosyne’s scope model is collection-name based, while Public’s is row-scoped and path-stable
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19025:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne derives a project collection from the directory basename and reserves a separate global collection. Public instead stores scope on each row (`tenant_id`, `user_id`, `agent_id`, `session_id`, `shared_space_id`) and builds logical identity from spec folder, canonical path, anchor, and scoped hash when needed.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19026:- **Why it matters for us**: Mnemosyne’s model is ergonomically simple, but it is weaker as a canonical data key. Basename-derived collections are collision-prone across similarly named repos, while Public’s model is designed for durable identity and finer isolation.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19027:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19029:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19031:### Finding 3: Public is built around one canonical row store plus derived search indexes
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19034:- **What it does**: `memory_index` is the source of truth; `vec_memories` is a derived vector table; `memory_fts` is a derived FTS5 table kept in sync by triggers. The live DB currently shows `2480` `memory_index` rows, `2480` `memory_fts` rows, `1893` parent rows, and `587` chunk children.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19035:- **Why it matters for us**: this is fundamentally different from Mnemosyne’s collection abstraction. Public is already a unified metadata store with multiple retrieval projections, so an Mnemosyne-style adoption would need to be a facade or adjunct, not a backend replacement.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19036:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19038:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19040:### Finding 4: Public preserves version history and active snapshots; Mnemosyne exposes only immediate CRUD at the plugin boundary
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19043:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne gives the agent `delete(id)` and nothing storage-visible about lineage. Public has append-only version insertion, `memory_lineage`, `active_memory_projection`, startup backfill for missing projections, and delete cleanup that removes vector/index side effects rather than only the primary row.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19044:- **Why it matters for us**: replacing Public’s storage model with a simpler delete-oriented contract would lose temporal resolution, active-version semantics, and integrity guarantees across companion indexes.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19045:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19047:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19049:### Finding 5: Public’s database is a full memory substrate, not just a recall index
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19052:- **What it does**: beyond retrieval, Public persists `working_memory`, `causal_edges`, `checkpoints`, `memory_summaries`, `memory_entities`, `entity_catalog`, `feedback_events`, `consumption_log`, and more. The live DB currently has `3246` causal edges, `1844` summaries, `69602` entity links, `16257` catalog entities, and only `176` rows with `document_type='memory'` versus `2304` indexed spec artifacts.

That means the main transferable idea is ergonomic surfacing, not storage simplification.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19054:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19056:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19058:### Finding 6: Extension-coupled vector storage raises operability requirements that Mnemosyne’s wrapper does not address
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:19061:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne documents sqlite-vec and local embeddings, but the wrapper has no schema-health or migration surface. Public explicitly tracks schema version `25`, validates embedding dimensions, supports provider-specific DB variants, and rebuilds BM25 from DB state at startup. /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22079:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-001.md:48:- What it does: `generateAIConfigs()` builds one generic narrative summary and writes or appends it into assistant-specific files such as `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `codex.md`, and `AGENTS.md`. `generateProfileConfig()` then creates tighter tool-specific variants, with the Claude profile explicitly instructing the assistant to read `.codesight/CODESIGHT.md` first and use narrow MCP tools for routes, schema, and blast radius.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22098:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-025.md:19:What it does: CodeSight's plugin contract is real in types but lightly proven in use, and its own conclusion is that untested plugin hooks are not a credible extension story.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22113:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-017.md:33:- What it does: profile mode rewrites `.cursorrules`, `codex.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and `.windsurfrules` directly. /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22115:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-017.md:42:- What it does: the Claude profile literally instructs the assistant to call `codesight_get_summary`, `codesight_get_routes`, `codesight_get_blast_radius`, and `codesight_get_schema`.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22117:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-017.md:51:- What it does: the Claude profile says "This saves ~N tokens per conversation" using the unrounded `result.tokenStats.saved.toLocaleString()`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22129:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-008.md:48:- What it does: `formatter.ts:290` writes "this file is ~X tokens. Without it, AI exploration would cost ~Y tokens. **Saves ~Z tokens per conversation.**" in `CODESIGHT.md`, with all three values passed through `roundTo100()` so the displayed numbers always end in `00` to signal estimation. But `ai-config.ts:213` writes "This saves ~${result.tokenStats.saved.toLocaleString()} tokens per conversation." into the Claude profile file using the raw, unrounded number — which can show values like `12,847` and read like a real measurement.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22130:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-008.md:49:- Why it matters for Code_Environment/Public: This is a small but meaningful UX inconsistency: the same upstream value is rounded for presentation in one surface and quoted unrounded in another, despite both being downstream consumers of the same heuristic formula. If we adopt the per-tool profile pattern (iter 4 finding 2), we should normalize the rounding rule across all surfaces — either always round-to-100 (signaling estimate) or always show raw (only honest if the formula is honest, which it is not). Pick rounding.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22140:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-009.md:30:- What it does: The CLI parser accepts `-o/--output`, `-d/--depth`, `--init`, `--watch`, `--hook`, `--html`, `--open`, `--mcp`, `--json`, `--benchmark`, `--profile <tool>`, `--blast <file>`, `--telemetry`, `--eval`, `-v/--version`, `-h/--help`, plus a positional directory argument. After parsing, `loadConfig(root)` is merged with CLI overrides only for `maxDepth`, `outputDir`, and `profile`; the rest stay as runtime booleans/strings outside the config object.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22141:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-009.md:58:- Why it matters for Code_Environment/Public: This is a clean "skip work, don't filter results" pattern that's worth borrowing wholesale. It pairs naturally with the future possibility of replacing a built-in detector with a plugin (disable the built-in, enable the plugin), and avoids paying the runtime cost of detection just to throw it away.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22142:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-009.md:66:- What it does: `CodesightConfig` exposes `plugins?: CodesightPlugin[]`; each plugin has a required `name`, optional async `detector(files, project)`, and optional async `postProcessor(result)`. Plugin detectors run after all built-ins, and can only merge additional `routes`, `schemas`, `components`, and `middleware` into the in-memory result set before contract enrichment/output. Post-processors run after `scan()` returns and can replace the final `ScanResult`. Within the files read, there are **no in-tree plugin implementations or plugin/disableDetectors tests** (`rg` over `external/tests` returned no matches), so third-party extensibility is inferred from the typed config-module surface rather than demonstrated by fixtures/tests.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22143:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/iterations/iteration-009.md:67:- Why it matters for Code_Environment/Public: Third-party detectors are possible if a user's config module imports or constructs plugin objects, but this is not a discovered package/plugin registry. Post-processors are a real extension point in code, not obviously vestigial, though they are currently unexercised in the visible test surface. For Public, the lesson is: plugin contracts that aren't tested aren't real. If we add plugin hooks, ship at least one in-tree fixture exercising them.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22308:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/findings-registry.json:2053:      "text": "Why it matters for Code_Environment/Public: This is a clean \"skip work, don't filter results\" pattern that's worth borrowing wholesale. It pairs naturally with the future possibility of replacing a built-in detector with a plugin (disable the built-in, enable the plugin), and avoids paying the runtime cost of detection just to throw it away.",
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22312:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/findings-registry.json:3481:      "text": "What it does: profile mode rewrites `.cursorrules`, `codex.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and `.windsurfrules` directly. It also writes `AGENTS.md` at repo root when absent in default generation mode.",
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22314:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/findings-registry.json:3487:      "text": "What it does: the Claude profile literally instructs the assistant to call `codesight_get_summary`, `codesight_get_routes`, `codesight_get_blast_radius`, and `codesight_get_schema`.",
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22316:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/findings-registry.json:3493:      "text": "What it does: the Claude profile says \"This saves ~N tokens per conversation\" using the unrounded `result.tokenStats.saved.toLocaleString()`.",
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22318:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/findings-registry.json:3511:      "text": "Why it matters for Code_Environment/Public: Public should adopt the profile-overlay pattern, not these literal tool names. Hardcoding non-existent tools into a generated profile creates broken assistant guidance.",
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22319:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/002-codesight/research/findings-registry.json:4009:      "text": "What it does: watch mode implies more incrementalism than it has, MCP query tools write `.codesight/` on disk, profile generation mutates root assistant files, and token messaging regains false precision outside `CODESIGHT.md`.",
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:22762:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/026-graph-and-context-optimization/001-research-graph-context-systems/research/research.md:54:Claudest remains the most composition-friendly pattern source for Public, but v2 now has a much sharper reason for saying so. It still does not mean “best portable source code”: the license story remains incomplete in this checkout, the host assumptions remain Claude-plugin-shaped, and the producer side still omits some analytics-grade fields. What it does mean is that Claudest’s strongest ideas already land inside one owner Public has, and the 20-iteration continuation converted those ideas into a packet-ordered implementation lane instead of leaving them as generic “adopt now” advice. The packet now points to one concrete first move inside Public’s continuity/analytics track: a shared FTS capability helper plus forced-degrade tests, followed by a bounded Stop-hook metadata patch, a reader-owned analytics model, an additive cached-summary fast path, an explicit verifier/discoverer workflow split, and finally portable token-observability contracts. Cached summaries can still be lossy and wrong, startup selection can still be heuristic, and dashboard-grade spend views can still overstate certainty when defaults or estimated token classes are not visibly labeled. That mix keeps Claudest as the primary reference for Public’s next implementation wave, but only if Public imports the humility, boundary discipline, and acceptance-gate logic alongside the feature shape. /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26010:## Focus
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26013:## Findings
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26014:### Finding 1: Mnemosyne exposes a deliberately tiny plugin surface, not a full memory platform API
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26017:- **What it does**: the external repo returns one OpenCode plugin object with exactly five tools plus one compaction hook; there is no HTTP surface, no MCP server, and no secondary registration layer. By contrast, Public’s memory server test suite locks `TOOL_DEFINITIONS.length` at 43.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26018:- **Why it matters for us**: Mnemosyne’s value on the API side is ergonomic minimalism, not capability breadth. It is a thin agent-facing facade over a backend binary, whereas Public already exposes a broad operational surface.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26019:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26020:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26022:### Finding 2: The CLI bridge is safely implemented, but operationally under-instrumented
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26025:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne shells out with `Bun.spawn(["mnemosyne", ...args])`, avoids shell interpolation, captures both stdout and stderr, and returns a friendly missing-binary message. But the wrapper only exposes `init`, `search`, `add`, and `delete`; it has no health, status, schema, or startup-readiness tool.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26026:- **Why it matters for us**: the argv-array bridge is worth copying if we ever front an external memory binary, but the missing operational tools would be a regression versus Public’s `ccc_status`, `session_bootstrap`, and richer MCP diagnostics.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26027:- **Recommendation**: adopt now
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26028:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26030:### Finding 3: Mnemosyne’s project/global split is ergonomic, but the actual scope key is weak
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26033:- **What it does**: the wrapper derives project scope from the current directory basename, special-cases `global` to `default`, auto-inits the project collection on load, and lazily inits global on first global write. Public instead exposes explicit `specFolder`, `tenantId`, `userId`, `agentId`, `sharedSpaceId`, and `sessionId` scope parameters.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26034:- **Why it matters for us**: the two-surface ergonomics are attractive, but basename-derived identity is collision-prone and too coarse for Public’s governed and session-aware memory model.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26035:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26036:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26038:### Finding 4: Mnemosyne has no profile separation; Public does
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26041:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne offers one fixed tool family and one fixed compaction prompt block. Public supports response `profile` values on `memory_context`, intent-to-profile auto-routing, and runtime-level profile separation in `.codex/config.toml` (`context`, `research`, `review`, `write`, etc.).
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26042:- **Why it matters for us**: Mnemosyne’s simplicity is nice for adoption, but it cannot express Public’s profile-aware recovery and formatting contracts. Adopting it as-is would flatten a capability Public already uses for routing, safety, and UX.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26043:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26044:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26046:### Finding 5: The compaction hook is the most transferable idea, but Public’s implementation substrate is stronger
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26049:- **What it does**: Mnemosyne injects a static memory-usage checklist into `experimental.session.compacting`. Public’s compact-code-graph plugin already does compaction injection too, but through a cached bridge transport plan, with dedupe checks and a plugin status tool.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26050:- **Why it matters for us**: the novel reusable part is not “compaction hook exists” but “memory-tool reminders survive compaction directly in prompt text.” Public can add that guidance inside its existing transport-plan architecture instead of copying Mnemosyne’s thinner standalone pattern.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26051:- **Recommendation**: adopt now

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26054:### Finding 6: Mnemosyne’s hybrid retrieval and offline-first story are mostly backend contract, not wrapper logic
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26057:- **What it does**: the wrapper only quotes the query and calls `mnemosyne search`; BM25, sqlite-vec, RRF, ONNX local inference, and the `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5` choice are README-level backend claims. Public already has hybrid `memory_search`, session-aware routing, and separately positions CocoIndex as semantic code search via CLI plus one MCP tool.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26058:- **Why it matters for us**: there is no evidence here for a superior retrieval algorithm at the wrapper layer. The actionable delta is surface design and first-run UX, not replacing Public’s retrieval core with Mnemosyne’s unseen backend.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/004-opencode-mnemosyne-main/research/research.md:26135:- **Recommeode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:175:- Why it matters: Public has compaction-oriented structural transport, but it does not currently enforce a comparable memory-preservation checkpoint before context collapse.
