/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190838:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:280:- **Impact**: high / medium / low
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190841:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10563:- **What it does**: `tool_status()` returns drawer counts plus two embedded instruction payloads: `PALACE_PROTOCOL` and `AAAK_SPEC`. The protocol explicitly tells the agent to call status on wake-up, query before answering, write a diary after each session, and invalidate stale KG facts before adding new ones. This makes the first memory call double as an operational contract.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190842:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10564:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the cleanest MemPalace agent-integration idea in the codebase. It reduces dependency on separate prompt docs because the memory surface itself teaches the right behavior. Public already has stronger startup guidance in MCP startup instructions and `session_bootstrap`, but it does not currently make one memory-facing tool return such a tight “how to use memory safely” contract.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190843:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10565:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190844:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10566:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190846:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10570:- **What it does**: MemPalace implements hooks twice: shell hooks for Claude/Codex install docs, and a Python `hooks_cli.py` layer that already abstracts `session-start`, `stop`, and `precompact` for multiple harnesses. The stop hook counts user messages, blocks every `SAVE_INTERVAL`, and emits a save instruction. The precompact hook always blocks and tells the agent to save everything before context loss. Optional `MEMPAL_DIR` auto-ingest exists, but the normal path tells the agent to classify and file the session itself.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190847:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10571:- **Why it matters for us**: The reusable value is not the exact shell scripts; it is the timing contract. MemPalace proves that passive capture can sit outside one model vendor and work as a harness-level preservation mechanism. The weakness is that once blocked, safety depends on the agent correctly choosing categories and scope with no governed boundaries.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190848:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10572:- **Recommendation**: adopt now
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190849:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10573:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190851:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10577:- **What it does**: The real source-backed multi-agent feature is `mempalace_diary_write/read`, which stores each agent’s journal under `wing_<agent>/room=diary`. There is no source-backed `mempalace_list_agents` tool, no agent registry in the MCP tool table, and no enforcement that an agent reads only its own diary or avoids other wings.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190852:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10578:- **Why it matters for us**: This is a useful reminder that per-agent memory can start as simple namespaced journals, but it is not enough for multi-agent safety. MemPalace’s README sells stronger agent specialization than the implementation currently proves. For Public, this means we should treat diary-per-agent as a lightweight UX idea, not as an isolation or trust boundary.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190853:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10579:- **Recommendation**: reject
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190854:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10580:- **Impact**: high
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190856:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10584:- **What it does**: Scoping is mostly `wing` and `room` metadata. Search, L2 recall, and L3 search all just build `where` filters on those fields. Conversation mining defaults the wing from the folder name if none is passed. Project mining routes files into rooms via folder/filename/keyword heuristics, and on re-mine it deletes all existing drawers for a source file before re-inserting fresh chunks.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190857:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10585:- **Why it matters for us**: This is good human-facing narrowing, but it is not safe scope governance. There is no tenant/user/agent/shared-space model, no cursor scoping, and no protected boundary between “my project” and “your project” beyond labels. The upside is ergonomic: the wing/room vocabulary is memorable and agent-friendly. The downside is that it is easy to mis-file or over-share unless another layer enforces scope.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190858:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10586:- **Recommendation**: prototype later
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190859:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10587:- **Impact**: medium
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190861:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10591:- **What it does**: Public’s retrieval path normalizes scope across `tenantId`, `userId`, `agentId`, `sessionId`, and `sharedSpaceId`, binds continuation cursors to that scope, supports session dedup and intent-to-profile routing, and emits recovery hints. Startup instructions already advertise `session_bootstrap`, `session_resume`, and structural recovery order. Save authority is explicit in `generate-context.js`, where the CLI target spec folder is authoritative. Compaction transport is also already externalized into the compact-code-graph plugin, which injects transport blocks at message and compaction boundaries.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190862:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-007.md:10592:- **Why it matters for us**: On agent integration and project safety, Public is ahead. MemPalace contributes a cleaner, more memorable behavioral surface, but not a safer one. The transferable parts are the small ones: one explicit memory protocol surface, and harness-level passive save timing. The scoping and multi-agent model should not be imported wholesale.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190947:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9752:- **Why it matters for us**: The big shift is representational pluralism. If we need fact-time validity, it should likely live in its own bounded fact plane rather than being forced into causal links, search metadata, or the main memory row shape.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190948:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9753:- **Recommendation**: prototype later

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190951:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9758:- **What it does**: MemPalace exposes many overlapping write authorities: direct drawer writes, diary writes, KG writes, AI-directed hook saves, and optional hook auto-ingest. Public is stricter: JSON-primary save is the canonical path, explicit target spec folder wins, direct spec-folder mode is rejected, and session recovery authority is explicitly preserved by `session_bootstrap`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190952:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9759:- **Why it matters for us**: The paradigm shift is to architect memory around a few clear authority owners: who decides where memory is saved, who owns session recovery truth, who injects compaction transport, and who is allowed to write derived fact state. That is a better scaling principle than adding more tools.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190953:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9760:- **Recommendation**: adopt now

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190956:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9765:- **What it does**: MemPalace makes people/projects/wings a first-class user-facing taxonomy from the start. Public instead grounds retrieval in governed scope fields like `tenantId`, `userId`, `agentId`, `sessionId`, and `sharedSpaceId`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190957:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9766:- **Why it matters for us**: The shift is not “copy wings.” It is to split identity into two planes: machine-trustworthy internal scope and optional human-friendly aliases/navigation. That would give us MemPalace’s ergonomic browsing without weakening governed retrieval.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190958:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9767:- **Recommendation**: prototype later

Public already encodes stricter guardrails in structured save contracts and confidence floors.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:190962:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-013.md:9773:- **Why it matters for us**: A memory system is not trustworthy if its interfaces blur what is stored, what is derived, what is experimental, and what is benchmark-only. Evidence tiering needs to be part of the product contract, not just a doc habit.

Public’s current compaction transport and JSON-primary `generate-context.js` path are much more deterministic.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191122:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-018.md:7115:- **Why it matters for us**: The reusable idea is strong: one surface can teach memory behavior, not just expose health. The safe version is a short, stable rule set, not a second operating manual.

That split is real. But `kg_add` does not require source evidence, contradiction detection is not actually wired into KG ops, and `invalidate` updates all matching live triples with no stronger review step.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191127:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-018.md:7122:- **Why it matters for us**: This is the one new architecture that Public genuinely lacks. The risk is governance, not mechanics: uncited fact insertion, ambiguous invalidation, silent drift between fact rows and verbatim memory, and agent-written “truth” that outruns its evidence. If we build this, it needs mandatory citations, authority tiers, correction workflows, and separation from ordinary memory writes.

The repo’s own correction note says the famous “palace boost” was mostly metadata filtering, and benchmark notes show roomed routing still trailing the stronger hybrid no-rooms baseline.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191132:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-018.md:7129:- **Why it matters for us**: If Public adopted this whole taxonomy, we would be buying label governance, reindex churn, room drift, fuzzy routing mistakes, and operator overhead for a capability that mostly repackages filtering we already have via scope, context types, and graph/search tools. The main thing that could go wrong is spending real product complexity on a memorable metaphor that does not improve truthfulness or recovery enough to justify itself.

The write path itself is weakly protected: `mempalace_add_drawer` uses deterministic IDs, but it does not actually call the semantic duplicate checker before writing.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191138:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-018.md:7183:- **Why it matters for us**: If we copy this pattern into Public, the biggest failure mode is a false sense of safety: the runtime is interrupted, but preservation quality still depends on the model following instructions correctly. That can yield duplicated memories, noisy categorization, partial saves, or blocked UX with no durable improvement. Public’s current compaction transport and JSON-primary `generate-context.js` path are much more deterministic.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191186:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-003.md:8411:- **What it does**: The documented CLI presents `init` as guided onboarding plus AAAK bootstrap, but `cmd_init()` only runs entity scan, room detection, and config init; the actual interactive onboarding flow lives separately in `run_onboarding()` and is never called by the CLI entrypoint. /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191191:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-003.md:8418:- **What it does**: MemPalace negotiates `initialize`, serves `tools/list`, and dispatches `tools/call` from one `TOOLS` dict of 19 entries, coercing basic numeric types and returning each result as JSON text. Logs go to `stderr`, protocol payloads go to `stdout`, which is handshake-clean. By contrast, Public’s current MCP surface is schema-driven and much broader, with dozens of typed tool definitions and centralized dispatch.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191192:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-003.md:8419:- **Why it matters for us**: The good idea here is transport simplicity and stderr discipline. The limitation is that capability separation, response shaping, and policy routing all live outside the protocol layer.

Gemini support is pushed into an example/setup guide rather than a real runtime branch. Public, by contrast, already has explicit runtime separation and transport indirection in the compact-code-graph plugin to keep host/runtime boundaries clean.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191202:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-003.md:8433:- **Why it matters for us**: MemPalace’s cross-client story is weaker in code than in docs. Public should not copy the “one README, many hosts” framing unless each host path is source-backed.

The risk is governance, not mechanics: uncited fact insertion, ambiguous invalidation, silent drift between fact rows and verbatim memory, and agent-written “truth” that outruns its evidence. If we build this, it needs mandatory citations, authority tiers, correction workflows, and separation from ordinary memory writes.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191478:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-019.md:6796:- **What it does**: MemPalace really does return verbatim drawer text at retrieval, but ingest is not uniformly “store everything untouched”: project files are chunked into 800-char drawers, conversation chunks collapse to exchange pairs or truncated response groups, and “general” mode heuristically selects typed memories.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191479:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-019.md:6797:- **Why it matters for us**: The right lesson for Public is not to replace JSON-primary curated saves with whole-transcript mining. /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191483:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-019.md:6803:- **What it does**: MemPalace exposes a clean L0/L1/L2/L3 contract, but the code path is thinner than the README framing. `wake_up()` reads `identity.txt` plus an L1 summary capped at 3200 chars; the “top moments” ranking falls back to default importance because the main miners do not populate the weight fields L1 looks for. The onboarding-generated AAAK bootstrap files are also separate from `layers.py`.

The interface is promising; the ranking engine is not yet strong enough to copy directly.

But `kg_add` accepts uncited writes, contradiction handling is explicitly not wired into KG ops, and invalidation updates any matching live triple without a stronger review gate.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191489:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-019.md:6811:- **Why it matters for us**: Public genuinely lacks this architecture today. It is the clearest long-term differentiator from ordinary memory search, but it must be built with mandatory citations, authority tiers, correction review, and fact-versus-verbatim separation from day one.

That is not “unfiltered raw memory”; it is selective routing and reduction. Public is also selective, but it makes that explicit through trigger filtering and save quality controls instead of presenting the result as untouched raw capture.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191918:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-002.md:15744:- **What it does**: A drawer is just raw document text plus light metadata such as `wing`, `room`, `source_file`, `chunk_index`, `added_by`, `filed_at`, and sometimes `source_mtime`, `ingest_mode`, or `extract_mode`. IDs are deterministic, but the strategy changes by ingest path: project/convo mining key off `source_file + chunk_index`, while MCP manual filing keys off `wing + room + content[:100]`.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191919:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-002.md:15745:- **Why it matters for us**: This preserves verbatim text well, but it has no built-in parent/child chunk graph, active-version pointer, or append-only lineage model. Public’s `memory_index` plus chunk/lineage tables are materially richer.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/research.md:191920:.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/005-mempalace/research/iterations/iteration-002.md:15746:- **Recommendation**: prototype later

Conversation mining skips solely on `source_file` existence. MCP exposes a semantic `mempalace_check_duplicate` tool, but `mempalace_add_drawer` does not call it; it only checks for an existing deterministic ID.

===== 003-modus-memory-main:9762-9882 =====
# Iteration 020: FINAL SYNTHESIS

## Focus
FINAL SYNTHESIS: Classify EVERY finding as adopt-now / prototype-later / new-feature-needed / reject. Executive summary.

**Executive summary:** Borrow **Modus’s operator surfaces**, not its weaker retrieval shortcuts. **Adopt now:** graded `memory_review`, doctor-style summary, and a strict one-retrieval-core rule. **New feature needed:** authoritative `memory_due` and a durable proposal inbox. **Prototype later:** connected-doc appendix, weak-result lexical fallback, and content-level contradiction linting. **Reject:** fuzzy result-cache reuse, permissive markdown ingestion, default write-on-read as policy, and unenforced trust-stage metadata.

## Findings

### Finding 1: Explicit graded review is the best immediate transfer
- **Source**: `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:885-897`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:160-217`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/cognitive/fsrs-scheduler.ts:39-43,65-71,197-215`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts:298-316`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/checkpoints.ts:648-790`
- **What it does**: Modus exposes `memory_reinforce`, but only as a success-only reinforce action. Public already has the stronger primitive: graded FSRS review (`AGAIN/HARD/GOOD/EASY`) plus computed `nextReviewDate`, yet the exposed adjacent tool is only `memory_validate(wasUseful)`, which adjusts confidence rather than recording a real review event.
- **Why it matters for us**: This closes the clearest control-plane gap without changing retrieval architecture. It also makes any later review queue trustworthy because review history would record hard recalls and lapses, not only “useful / not useful.”
- **Recommendation**: adopt now
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 2: A doctor-style summary should ship beside review
- **Source**: `external/cmd/modus-memory/doctor.go:13-242`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-crud-health.ts:378-594`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts:236-273`
- **What it does**: Modus’s `doctor` turns vault health into a one-screen operator report. Public already has deeper health and repair machinery—FTS rebuild, orphan cleanup, degraded/healthy state, confirmation-gated repair—but exposes it as a richer technical envelope.
- **Why it matters for us**: This is mostly presentation work, not backend work. It improves operator trust immediately while preserving Public’s stronger repair semantics underneath.
- **Recommendation**: adopt now
- **Impact**: medium

### Finding 3: Keep one retrieval core; Modus’s split fact-search paths are a warning
- **Source**: `external/internal/index/indexer.go:287-340`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:290-337`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:273-317`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:771-809`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/search/pipeline/index.ts:1-32`
- **What it does**: Modus has multiple fact-search contracts for the same memory objects: `Index.SearchFacts`, a separate in-memory `factStore`, and `Vault.SearchFacts` fallback behavior. Public routes `memory_search` through one pipeline contract via `executePipeline`.
- **Why it matters for us**: This is the strongest architectural lesson from Modus’s weaknesses. Public should keep specialized search surfaces as thin wrappers over the canonical pipeline instead of growing parallel ranking rules that will drift.
- **Recommendation**: adopt now
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 4: `memory_due` is real product value, but it needs an authoritative due-state contract first
- **Source**: `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:273-317,856-897`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:64-157,160-217`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/cognitive/fsrs-scheduler.ts:65-71,177-215`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:519-520`
- **What it does**: Modus visibly ties search recall, reinforce, decay, and archive to one fact state. Public already stores `stability`, `difficulty`, `last_review`, `review_count`, and opt-in access effects, and computes `nextReviewDate`, but does not expose an operator-facing due queue.
- **Why it matters for us**: This is the biggest missing workflow surface in Public. But it should not ship until “due” is defined as either persisted state (`next_review_at`) or a deterministic derivation from existing FSRS fields.
- **Recommendation**: NEW FEATURE
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 5: Durable proposal inboxes are the best non-retrieval idea Modus has
- **Source**: `external/internal/vault/prs.go:10-118`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:681-777`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/save/reconsolidation-bridge.ts:417-452`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/checkpoints.ts:681-790`
- **What it does**: Modus persists risky knowledge changes as markdown PR artifacts, then merge/reject outcomes reinforce or weaken linked beliefs. Public already produces advisory reconsolidation recommendations and confidence feedback, but the recommendation is transient and not stored as a durable review object.
- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s next gap is operator workflow, not mutation safety. A persistent inbox for reconsolidation, supersession, promotion, and deprecation proposals would let existing confidence and mutation systems work as a real review loop.
- **Recommendation**: NEW FEATURE
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 6: Connected-doc hints are worth prototyping only as an explanation appendix
- **Source**: `external/internal/index/crossref.go:154-214,248-280`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:75-101,901-924`
- **What it does**: Modus builds lightweight subject/entity/tag adjacency and appends connected docs that did not make the main ranked list. The weighting is simple and fixed (`subject 3`, `entity 2`, `tag 1`).
- **Why it matters for us**: The transferable part is explanation, not ranking. Public can test a “related memories” appendix without diluting stronger graph-backed or hybrid scoring paths.
- **Recommendation**: prototype later
- **Impact**: medium

### Finding 7: Lexical-only expansion belongs only in weak-result recovery
- **Source**: `external/internal/librarian/search.go:10-52`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:28-58,280-299`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:525-529,771-809`
- **What it does**: Modus asks the Librarian for 3-5 keyword variants, searches each, deduplicates, and caps results. It is lightweight, but ungrounded and union-first.
- **Why it matters for us**: Public already has a more complex retrieval pipeline, so copying this as a mainline branch would mostly add noise and latency. The only credible transfer is a tightly bounded fallback when hybrid retrieval is weak.
- **Recommendation**: prototype later
- **Impact**: low

### Finding 8: Content-level contradiction and duplicate-fact linting is still worth a prototype
- **Source**: `external/cmd/modus-memory/doctor.go:42-158`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-crud-health.ts:455-555`
- **What it does**: Modus’s `doctor` explicitly flags missing `subject`/`predicate`, duplicate `subject+predicate` pairs, and contradictory values for the same pair. Public’s current health surface is stronger on infrastructure integrity than on fact-content linting.
- **Why it matters for us**: This complements Public’s existing infra health checks instead of replacing them. It is one of the few Modus hygiene ideas that adds net-new value.
- **Recommendation**: prototype later
- **Impact**: medium

### Finding 9: Reject Modus’s fuzzy Jaccard result-cache contract
- **Source**: `external/internal/index/cache.go:10-17,41-119`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:502-529,718-755`
- **What it does**: Modus reuses cached result sets on exact hash hits or Jaccard-similar query term sets. Public’s search surface has too many scoring knobs—scope, archived filtering, session/causal boost, rerank, quality thresholds, trace/profile flags—for fuzzy query reuse to be safe.
- **Why it matters for us**: This is the wrong cache contract for Public. Similar text is not enough to guarantee equivalent retrieval intent or scoring context.
- **Recommendation**: reject
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 10: Reject Modus’s permissive markdown parse/write contract
- **Source**: `external/internal/markdown/parser.go:98-159,161-186`; `external/internal/markdown/writer.go:10-52`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts:220-220`
- **What it does**: Modus treats malformed YAML as body, skips parse failures during scans, and writes markdown directly with minimal validation. That is good for a personal vault, but it optimizes for permissiveness over authoritative ingestion.
- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s memory layer is intentionally more governed. Regressing to Modus’s permissive storage contract would weaken memory integrity for little gain.
- **Recommendation**: reject
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 11: Reject default write-on-read as Public’s default policy
- **Source**: `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:311-317`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:188-217`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:519-520,797-802`
- **What it does**: Modus treats every returned fact as a successful recall and asynchronously reinforces it. Public already supports access effects, but keeps them explicit with `trackAccess=false` by default.
- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s graded FSRS model is stronger than Modus’s success-only reinforce loop. Default write-on-read would blur retrieval and review, inflate successful-recall history, and make future due-state less trustworthy.
- **Recommendation**: reject
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 12: Reject trust-stage metadata unless it becomes real gating
- **Source**: `external/internal/vault/trust.go:11-82`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:610-635,681-777`; repo search on `external/internal/**/*.go` shows trust-stage calls only in trust read/write surfaces
- **What it does**: Modus persists trust stage and exposes get/set tools, but current code does not use that state to gate PR or other mutation tools. It is posture metadata, not enforced runtime policy.
- **Why it matters for us**: Public should not copy symbolic governance. If autonomy stages are added, they must actually gate review, proposal, or mutation flows.
- **Recommendation**: reject
- **Impact**: medium

    16	// Field weights — title matches are more valuable than body matches.
    17	// Validated by ByteRover's benchmark: title 3x, path 1.5x achieves 96% LoCoMo.

    21		2.0, // subject

    37	// posting records a term occurrence in a specific document field.
    38	type posting struct {

    44	// bm25Engine holds the inverted index and document stats for BM25 scoring.
    45	type bm25Engine struct {

    48		avgLens  [6]float64           // average field lengths across corpus

    50	}

    52	// newBM25Engine builds an inverted index from the loaded documents.
    53	func newBM25Engine(docs []document) *bm25Engine {
    54		e := &bm25Engine{
    55			postings: make(map[string][]posting),
    56			docLens:  make([][6]int, len(docs)),
    57			numDocs:  len(docs),
    58		}
    59	
    60		var totalLens [6]int64
    61	
    62		for docID, doc := range docs {

    64				doc.Path,
    65				doc.Source,
    66				doc.Subject,
    67				doc.Title,
    68				doc.Tags,
    69				doc.Body,
    70			}

    72			for fieldID, text := range fields {
    73				tokens := tokenize(text)
    74				e.docLens[docID][fieldID] = len(tokens)
    75				totalLens[fieldID] += int64(len(tokens))
    76	
    77				// Count term frequencies
    78				tf := make(map[string]int)
    79				for _, t := range tokens {
    80					tf[t]++
    81				}
    82	
    83				for term, count := range tf {
    84					e.postings[term] = append(e.postings[term], posting{
    85						docID: docID,
    86						field: fieldID,
    87						tf:    count,
    88					})
    89				}
    90			}
    91		}
    92	
    93		// Compute average field lengths
    94		for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
    95			if e.numDocs > 0 {
    96				e.avgLens[i] = float64(totalLens[i]) / float64(e.numDocs)
    97			}
    98		}

   103	// search scores all documents against the query and returns top results.
   104	func (e *bm25Engine) search(query string, limit int) []scoredDoc {
   105		queryTerms := tokenize(query)
   106		if len(queryTerms) == 0 {

   108		}
   109	
   110		// Accumulate scores per document
   111		scores := make(map[int]float64)
   112

   117				posts = e.prefixMatch(term)
   118				if len(posts) == 0 {

   121			}
   122	
   123			// IDF: log((N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5) + 1)
   124			df := e.docFreq(term)
   125			idf := math.Log((float64(e.numDocs)-float64(df)+0.5)/(float64(df)+0.5) + 1.0)
   126	
   127			for _, p := range posts {
   128				// BM25 per-field score with field weight
   129				dl := float64(e.docLens[p.docID][p.field])

   137				denominator := tf + bm25K1*(1-bm25B+bm25B*dl/avgDl)
   138	
   139				score := idf * (numerator / denominator) * fieldWeights[p.field]
   140				scores[p.docID] += score
   141			}
   142		}
   143	
   144		// Sort by score descending
   145		var results []scoredDoc
   146		for docID, score := range scores {
   147			results = append(results, scoredDoc{docID: docID, score: score})
   148		}
   149		sort.Slice(results, func(i, j int) bool {
   150			return results[i].score > results[j].score
   151		})

   154			results = results[:limit]
   155		}

   160	func (e *bm25Engine) docFreq(term string) int {

   174		}
   175		var results []posting
   176		for term, posts := range e.postings {
   177			if strings.HasPrefix(term, prefix) {

   189	// tokenize splits text into lowercase tokens, removing punctuation.
   190	// Uses Porter-like stemming for common suffixes.
   191	func tokenize(text string) []string {
   192		text = strings.ToLower(text)
   193		var tokens []string
   194		var current strings.Builder
   195	
   196		for _, r := range text {
   197			if unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r) {
   198				current.WriteRune(r)
   199			} else {
   200				if current.Len() > 0 {
   201					token := current.String()
   202					if len(token) >= 2 { // skip single-char tokens
   203						tokens = append(tokens, stem(token))
   204					}
   205					current.Reset()
   206				}
   207			}
   208		}
   209		if current.Len() > 0 {
   210			token := current.String()
   211			if len(token) >= 2 {
   212				tokens = append(tokens, stem(token))
   213			}
   214		}
   215	
   216		return tokens
   217	}

   220	// just enough to match plurals and common verb forms.

   154	// Connected returns the full neighborhood of a query — union of subject, tag,
   155	// and entity matches, deduplicated by path, sorted by connection count.
   156	func (ci *crossIndex) Connected(query string, limit int) []DocRef {
   157		if limit <= 0 {
   158			limit = 20
   159		}
   160	
   161		terms := strings.Fields(strings.ToLower(query))
   162		if len(terms) == 0 {
   163			return nil
   164		}
   165	
   166		// Score each document by how many query terms connect to it
   167		scores := make(map[string]*DocRef)  // path → ref
   168		counts := make(map[string]float64)  // path → connection strength
   169	
   170		addRefs := func(refs []DocRef, weight float64) {
   171			for _, r := range refs {
   172				counts[r.Path] += weight
   173				if _, ok := scores[r.Path]; !ok {
   174					copy := r
   175					scores[r.Path] = &copy
   176				}
   177			}
   178		}
   179	
   180		for _, term := range terms {
   181			addRefs(ci.bySubject[term], 3.0) // subject match is strongest
   182			addRefs(ci.byEntity[term], 2.0)  // entity match is strong
   183			addRefs(ci.byTag[term], 1.0)     // tag match is weaker
   184		}
   185	
   186		// Also try the full query as a single key
   187		fullQuery := strings.Join(terms, " ")
   188		addRefs(ci.bySubject[fullQuery], 3.0)
   189		addRefs(ci.byEntity[fullQuery], 2.0)
   190	
   191		// Sort by connection strength
   192		type ranked struct {
   193			ref   *DocRef
   194			score float64
   195		}
   196		var results []ranked
   197		for path, ref := range scores {
   198			ref.Rank = counts[path]
   199			results = append(results, ranked{ref, counts[path]})
   200		}
   201		sort.Slice(results, func(i, j int) bool {
   202			return results[i].score > results[j].score
   203		})
   204	
   205		if len(results) > limit {
   206			results = results[:limit]
   207		}
   208	
   209		out := make([]DocRef, len(results))
   210		for i, r := range results {
   211			out[i] = *r.ref
   212		}
   213		return out
   214	}

   219	}

179677	## Assessment
179678	- New information ratio: 0.46
179679	- Questions addressed: markdown-first scaffold tradeoffs; checker composition and blind spots; freshness thresholds and git failure semantics; claim extraction behavior; targeted sync design; post-task scaffold growth; overlap with current Spec Kit validation and trust surfaces
179680	- Questions answered: adopt only static reference integrity now; prototype freshness only with explicit trust semantics; build repair briefs as a new feature; defer inventory-backed parity until a cross-surface model exists; reject auto-growth defaults and reject score-first health

179699	## Focus
179700	FINAL SYNTHESIS: Classify every major Mex mechanism as `adopt now`, `prototype later`, `NEW FEATURE`, or `reject`.
179701	
179702	Executive summary: Mex is strongest as a thin markdown-integrity layer, not as a replacement for Spec Kit Memory. The clear win is narrow static reference integrity for markdown surfaces. Freshness is worth prototyping only if we preserve Spec Kit’s explicit `exact` / `estimated` / `unknown` / blocked semantics. Targeted repair briefs are worth building as a new feature. Inventory-heavy parity checks need a broader abstraction first. Auto-growth and score-first health should stay out.

179707	- **What it does**: Mex extracts typed markdown claims from inline code, code blocks, and dependency headings, then runs zero-token checks for missing paths, dead frontmatter edges, and `patterns/INDEX.md` drift. 179712	### Finding 2: Dual freshness signals are useful, but only as supplemental trust metadata
179713	- **Source**: [staleness.ts](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/002-mex-main/external/src/drift/checkers/staleness.ts#L4), [git.ts](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/002-mex-main/external/src/git.ts#L12), [shared-payload.ts](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/context/shared-payload.ts#L22), [session-bootstrap.ts](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/session-bootstrap.ts#L219), [memory-triggers.ts](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-triggers.ts#L329)

197268	## Focus
197269	FINAL SYNTHESIS: Classify EVERY finding as adopt-now / prototype-later / new-feature-needed / reject. Executive summary.
197270	
197271	MemPalace contributes two near-term ideas worth carrying into Public now: a compaction-time structured save checkpoint and a short bootstrap hint layer that teaches memory behavior. Everything else should stay scoped: selective verbatim evidence retention and layered wake-up are worth prototyping, a temporal fact plane is a separate net-new feature track, and full taxonomy plus AAAK/diary-centric recall should be rejected as primary architecture. I used prior phase memory only to recover continuity; the findings below are based on current-turn source reads.

    90		// Check if query already cached — update results
    91		for i := range c.entries {
    92			if c.entries[i].query == query {
    93				c.entries[i].results = results
    94				c.entries[i].hits = c.counter
    95				return
    96			}
    97		}
    98	
    99		entry := cacheEntry{
   100			query:   query,
   101			terms:   termSet(query),
   102			results: results,
   103			hits:    c.counter,
   104		}
   105	
   106		if len(c.entries) >= cacheMaxEntries {
   107			// Evict LRU entry
   108			minIdx := 0
   109			minHits := c.entries[0].hits
   110			for i := 1; i < len(c.entries); i++ {
   111				if c.entries[i].hits < minHits {
   112					minHits = c.entries[i].hits
   113					minIdx = i
   114				}
   115			}
   116			c.entries[minIdx] = entry
   117		} else {
   118			c.entries = append(c.entries, entry)
   119		}
   120	}
   121	
   122	func hashQuery(q string) uint64 {
   123		h := fnv.New64a()
   124		h.Write([]byte(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(q))))
   125		return h.Sum64()
   126	}
   127	
   128	func termSet(query string) map[string]bool {
   129		terms := tokenize(query)
   130		set := make(map[string]bool, len(terms))
   131		for _, t := range terms {
   132			set[t] = true
   133		}
   134		return set
   135	}
   136	
   137	// jaccard computes the Jaccard similarity between two term sets.
   138	func jaccard(a, b map[string]bool) float64 {
   139		if len(a) == 0 && len(b) == 0 {
   140			return 0
   141		}
   142	
   143		intersection := 0
   144		for term := range a {
   145			if b[term] {
   146				intersection++
   147			}
   148		}
   149	
   150		union := len(a) + len(b) - intersection
   151		if union == 0 {
   152			return 0
   153		}
   154	
   155		return float64(intersection) / float64(union)
   156	}
   157	
   158	// sortByScore sorts results by score normalization: s / (1 + s) → [0, 1).
   159	// Higher is better. ByteRover uses this normalization for consistent thresholding.
   160	func normalizeScore(score float64) float64 {
   161		if score <= 0 {
   162			return 0
   163		}
   164		return score / (1.0 + score)
   165	}
   166	
   167	// filterOOD performs out-of-domain detection.
   168	// If significant query terms (>= 4 chars) are unmatched and top score
   169	// is below threshold, returns true (query is out of domain).
   170	func filterOOD(query string, results []scoredDoc, threshold float64) bool {
   171		if len(results) == 0 {
   172			return true
   173		}
   174	
   175		topNormalized := normalizeScore(results[0].score)
   176		if topNormalized >= threshold {
   177			return false
   178		}
   179	
   180		// Check if significant terms are all unmatched
   181		terms := tokenize(query)
   182		significant := 0
   183		for _, t := range terms {
   184			if len(t) >= 4 {
   185				significant++
   186			}
   187		}
   188	
   189		// If most terms are short (< 4 chars), don't filter
   190		if significant == 0 {
   191			return false
   192		}
   193	
   194		return topNormalized < threshold
   195	}
   196	
   197	// deduplicateResults removes duplicate paths, keeping the highest scored.
   198	func deduplicateResults(results []SearchResult) []SearchResult {
   199		seen := make(map[string]int) // path → index in output
   200		var deduped []SearchResult
   201	
   202		// Results should already be sorted by rank (best first)
   203		for _, r := range results {
   204			if _, exists := seen[r.Path]; !exists {
   205				seen[r.Path] = len(deduped)
   206				deduped = append(deduped, r)
   207			}
   208		}
   209	
   210		sort.Slice(deduped, func(i, j int) bool {
   211			return deduped[i].Rank > deduped[j].Rank
   212		})
   213	
   214		return deduped
   215	}

    57	func RankResults(query string, results []ResultSnippet, topN int) []int {

    73		}
    74

    76	return a JSON array of the most relevant result numbers (1-indexed), ordered by relevance.
    77	Return ONLY the JSON array of integers. No explanation.`
    78	
    79		user := fmt.Sprintf("Query: %q\nReturn the top %d most relevant results:\n\n%s",
    80			query, topN, sb.String())

    11	
    12	// FSRS (Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler) parameters for memory decay.
    13	// Dual-strength model: each fact has stability (how long until 90% recall drops)
    14	// and difficulty (how hard it is to retain). Inspired by LACP's Mycelium Network
    15	// and the FSRS-5 algorithm. Local adaptation: importance gates initial stability,
    16	// memory type gates difficulty, and access-based reinforcement resets the clock.
    17	
    18	// fsrsConfig holds per-importance FSRS parameters.
    19	type fsrsConfig struct {
    20		InitialStability float64 // days until R drops to 0.9 (S0)
    21		InitialDifficulty float64 // 0.0 (trivial) to 1.0 (very hard)
    22		Floor            float64 // minimum confidence (retrievability)
    23	}
    24	
    25	var fsrsConfigs = map[string]fsrsConfig{
    26		"critical": {InitialStability: 1e9, InitialDifficulty: 0, Floor: 1.0}, // never decays
    27		"high":     {InitialStability: 180, InitialDifficulty: 0.3, Floor: 0.3},
    28		"medium":   {InitialStability: 60, InitialDifficulty: 0.5, Floor: 0.1},
    29		"low":      {InitialStability: 14, InitialDifficulty: 0.7, Floor: 0.05},
    30	}
    31	
    32	// Memory type difficulty modifiers. Procedural knowledge is hardest to forget,
    33	// episodic is easiest (it's contextual and fades without reinforcement).
    34	var memoryTypeDifficultyMod = map[string]float64{
    35		"semantic":   -0.1, // easier to retain (general knowledge)
    36		"episodic":   +0.2, // harder to retain (context-dependent)
    37		"procedural": -0.3, // hardest to forget (muscle memory analog)
    38	}
    39	
    40	// fsrsRetrievability computes R(t) = (1 + t/(9*S))^(-1)
    41	// where t = elapsed days, S = stability. This is the FSRS power-law forgetting curve.
    42	// R=0.9 when t=S (by definition of stability).
    43	func fsrsRetrievability(elapsedDays, stability float64) float64 {
    44		if stability <= 0 {
    45			return 0
    46		}
    47		return math.Pow(1.0+elapsedDays/(9.0*stability), -1.0)
    48	}
    49	
    50	// fsrsNewStability computes updated stability after a successful recall.
    51	// S' = S * (1 + e^(w) * (11-D) * S^(-0.2) * (e^(0.05*(1-R)) - 1))
    52	// Simplified from FSRS-5. w=2.0 is the stability growth factor.
    53	func fsrsNewStability(oldStability, difficulty, retrievability float64) float64 {
    54		w := 2.0 // growth factor — higher means faster stability growth on recall
    55		d := difficulty * 10 // scale to 0-10 range
    56		growth := math.Exp(w) * (11.0 - d) * math.Pow(oldStability, -0.2) * (math.Exp(0.05*(1.0-retrievability)) - 1.0)
    57		newS := oldStability * (1.0 + growth)
    58		if newS < oldStability {
    59			newS = oldStability // stability never decreases on recall
    60		}
    61		return newS
    62	}
    63	
    64	// DecayFacts sweeps all fact files and applies FSRS-based confidence decay.
    65	// Confidence = retrievability R(t) = (1 + t/(9*S))^(-1), floored per importance.
    66	// Returns the number of facts updated.
    67	func (v *Vault) DecayFacts() (int, error) {
    68		docs, err := markdown.ScanDir(v.Path("memory", "facts"))
    69		if err != nil {
    70			return 0, err
    71		}
    72	
    73		now := time.Now()
    74		updated := 0
    75	
    76		for _, doc := range docs {
    77			conf := doc.GetFloat("confidence")
    78			importance := doc.Get("importance")
    79			if importance == "" {
    80				importance = "medium"
    81			}
    82	
    83			cfg, ok := fsrsConfigs[importance]
    84			if !ok {
    85				cfg = fsrsConfigs["medium"]
    86			}
    87	
    88			// Critical facts never decay
    89			if cfg.InitialStability >= 1e8 {
    90				continue
    91			}
    92	
    93			if conf <= cfg.Floor {
    94				continue
    95			}
    96	
    97			// Get or initialize stability
    98			stability := doc.GetFloat("stability")
    99			if stability <= 0 {
   100				stability = cfg.InitialStability
   101				// Apply memory type modifier to difficulty → affects initial stability
   102				memType := doc.Get("memory_type")
   103				if mod, ok := memoryTypeDifficultyMod[memType]; ok {
   104					adjustedDifficulty := cfg.InitialDifficulty + mod
   105					if adjustedDifficulty < 0 {
   106						adjustedDifficulty = 0
   107					}
   108					if adjustedDifficulty > 1.0 {
   109						adjustedDifficulty = 1.0
   110					}
   111					// Lower difficulty → higher stability
   112					stability = cfg.InitialStability * (1.0 + (0.5 - adjustedDifficulty))
   113				}
   114				doc.Set("stability", math.Round(stability*10) / 10)
   115				doc.Set("difficulty", cfg.InitialDifficulty)
   116			}
   117	
   118			// Calculate days since last access or creation
   119			lastAccessed := doc.Get("last_accessed")
   120			if lastAccessed == "" {
   121				lastAccessed = doc.Get("last_decayed")
   122			}
   123			if lastAccessed == "" {
   124				lastAccessed = doc.Get("created")
   125			}
   126			if lastAccessed == "" {
   127				continue
   128			}
   129	
   130			t, err := parseTime(lastAccessed)
   131			if err != nil {
   132				continue
   133			}
   134	
   135			elapsedDays := now.Sub(t).Hours() / 24
   136			if elapsedDays < 0.5 {
   137				continue // too recent to decay
   138			}
   139	
   140			// FSRS retrievability: R(t) = (1 + t/(9*S))^(-1)
   141			newConf := fsrsRetrievability(elapsedDays, stability)
   142			newConf = math.Max(cfg.Floor, newConf)
   143			newConf = math.Round(newConf*1000) / 1000
   144	
   145			if newConf == conf {
   146				continue
   147			}
   148	
   149			doc.Set("confidence", newConf)
   150			doc.Set("last_decayed", now.Format(time.RFC3339))
   151			if err := doc.Save(); err != nil {
   152				continue
   153			}
   154			updated++
   155		}
   156	
   157		return updated, nil
   158	}
   159	
   160	// ReinforceFact increases a fact's confidence and stability after a successful recall.
   161	// This is the FSRS "review" operation — accessing a fact proves it's still relevant,
   162	// so stability grows and confidence resets toward 1.0.
   163	func (v *Vault) ReinforceFact(relPath string) error {
   164		doc, err := v.Read(relPath)
   165		if err != nil {
   166			return err
   167		}
   168	
   169		now := time.Now()
   170		conf := doc.GetFloat("confidence")
   171		stability := doc.GetFloat("stability")
   172		difficulty := doc.GetFloat("difficulty")
   173	
   174		importance := doc.Get("importance")
   175		if importance == "" {
   176			importance = "medium"
   177		}
   178		cfg := fsrsConfigs[importance]
   179	
   180		// Initialize if missing
   181		if stability <= 0 {
   182			stability = cfg.InitialStability
   183		}
   184		if difficulty <= 0 {
   185			difficulty = cfg.InitialDifficulty
   186		}
   187	
   188		// Compute new stability: grows on each successful recall
   189		newStability := fsrsNewStability(stability, difficulty, conf)
   190	
   191		// Difficulty decreases slightly on successful recall (fact gets easier)
   192		newDifficulty := difficulty - 0.02
   193		if newDifficulty < 0.05 {
   194			newDifficulty = 0.05
   195		}
   196	
   197		// Confidence boost: asymptotic toward 1.0, small increment per access
   198		newConf := conf + (1.0-conf)*0.08
   199		if newConf > 0.99 {
   200			newConf = 0.99
   201		}
   202	
   203		// Track access count
   204		accessCount := 0
   205		if ac := doc.GetFloat("access_count"); ac > 0 {
   206			accessCount = int(ac)
   207		}
   208		accessCount++
   209	
   210		doc.Set("confidence", math.Round(newConf*1000)/1000)
   211		doc.Set("stability", math.Round(newStability*10)/10)
   212		doc.Set("difficulty", math.Round(newDifficulty*1000)/1000)
   213		doc.Set("last_accessed", now.Format(time.RFC3339))
   214		doc.Set("access_count", accessCount)
   215	
   216		return doc.Save()
   217	}
   218	
   219	// ArchiveStaleFacts marks facts below a confidence threshold as archived.
   220	// Returns the number of facts archived.
   221	func (v *Vault) ArchiveStaleFacts(threshold float64) (int, error) {
   222		if threshold <= 0 {
   223			threshold = 0.1
   224		}
   225	
   226		docs, err := markdown.ScanDir(v.Path("memory", "facts"))
   227		if err != nil {
   228			return 0, err
   229		}
   230	
   231		archived := 0
   232		for _, doc := range docs {
   233			// Skip already archived
   234			if doc.Get("archived") == "true" {
   235				continue
   236			}
   237			// Skip critical facts
   238			if doc.Get("importance") == "critical" {
   239				continue
   240			}
   241	
   242			conf := doc.GetFloat("confidence")
   243			if conf > 0 && conf < threshold {
   244				doc.Set("archived", true)
   245				doc.Set("archived_at", time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339))
   246				if err := doc.Save(); err != nil {
   247					continue
   248				}
   249				archived++
   250			}
   251		}
   252	
   253		return archived, nil
   254	}

   256	// TouchFact updates last_accessed on a fact, resetting its decay clock.
   257	func (v *Vault) TouchFact(relPath string) error {
   258		doc, err := v.Read(relPath)
   259		if err != nil {
   260			return err
   261		}
   262		doc.Set("last_accessed", time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339))
   263		return doc.Save()
   264	}

    49	// MergePR marks a PR as merged and reinforces all linked beliefs.

    51	func (v *Vault) MergePR(relPath, closedBy string) error {
    52		doc, err := v.Read(relPath)
    53		if err != nil {
    54			return fmt.Errorf("read PR: %w", err)
    55		}

    58		if status != "open" {
    59			return fmt.Errorf("PR is %s, not open — cannot merge", status)
    60		}
    61	
    62		doc.Set("status", "merged")
    63		doc.Set("closed_at", time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339))

   127	// parseStringList handles both Go string slices and YAML-formatted string lists.
   128	func parseStringList(s string) []string {
   129		// Handle YAML list format: [a, b, c]
   130		s = trimBrackets(s)
   131		if s == "" {
   132			return nil
   133		}
   134		parts := splitAndTrim(s, ",")
   135		return parts
   136	}
   137	
   138	func trimBrackets(s string) string {
   139		if len(s) >= 2 && s[0] == '[' && s[len(s)-1] == ']' {
   140			return s[1 : len(s)-1]
   141		}
   142		return s
   143	}
   144	
   145	func splitAndTrim(s, sep string) []string {
   146		var result []string
   147		for _, part := range splitString(s, sep) {
   148			trimmed := trimQuotes(trimSpace(part))
   149			if trimmed != "" {
   150				result = append(result, trimmed)
   151			}
   152		}
   153		return result
   154	}
   155	
   156	func splitString(s, sep string) []string {
   157		var parts []string
   158		for {
   159			i := indexOf(s, sep)
   160			if i < 0 {
   161				parts = append(parts, s)
   162				break
   163			}
   164			parts = append(parts, s[:i])
   165			s = s[i+len(sep):]
   166		}
   167		return parts
   168	}
   169	
   170	func indexOf(s, sub string) int {
   171		for i := 0; i <= len(s)-len(sub); i++ {
   172			if s[i:i+len(sub)] == sub {
   173				return i
   174			}
   175		}
   176		return -1
   177	}
   178	
   179	func trimSpace(s string) string {
   180		for len(s) > 0 && (s[0] == ' ' || s[0] == '\t' || s[0] == '\n') {
   181			s = s[1:]
   182		}
   183		for len(s) > 0 && (s[len(s)-1] == ' ' || s[len(s)-1] == '\t' || s[len(s)-1] == '\n') {
   184			s = s[:len(s)-1]
   185		}
   186		return s
   187	}
   188	
   189	func trimQuotes(s string) string {
   190		if len(s) >= 2 && ((s[0] == '"' && s[len(s)-1] == '"') || (s[0] == '\'' && s[len(s)-1] == '\'')) {
   191			return s[1 : len(s)-1]
   192		}
   193		return s
   194	}

  9764	## Focus
  9765	FINAL SYNTHESIS: Classify EVERY finding as adopt-now / prototype-later / new-feature-needed / reject. Executive summary.
  9766	
  9767	**Executive summary:** Borrow **Modus’s operator surfaces**, not its weaker retrieval shortcuts. **Adopt now:** graded `memory_review`, doctor-style summary, and a strict one-retrieval-core rule. **New feature needed:** authoritative `memory_due` and a durable proposal inbox. **Prototype later:** connected-doc appendix, weak-result lexical fallback, and content-level contradiction linting. **Reject:** fuzzy result-cache reuse, permissive markdown ingestion, default write-on-read as policy, and unenforced trust-stage metadata.
  9768	
  9769	## Findings
  9770	
  9771	### Finding 1: Explicit graded review is the best immediate transfer
  9772	- **Source**: `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:885-897`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:160-217`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/cognitive/fsrs-scheduler.ts:39-43,65-71,197-215`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts:298-316`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/checkpoints.ts:648-790`
  9773	- **What it does**: Modus exposes `memory_reinforce`, but only as a success-only reinforce action. Public already has the stronger primitive: graded FSRS review (`AGAIN/HARD/GOOD/EASY`) plus computed `nextReviewDate`, yet the exposed adjacent tool is only `memory_validate(wasUseful)`, which adjusts confidence rather than recording a real review event.
  9774	- **Why it matters for us**: This closes the clearest control-plane gap without changing retrieval architecture. It also makes any later review queue trustworthy because review history would record hard recalls and lapses, not only “useful / not useful.”
  9775	- **Recommendation**: adopt now
  9776	- **Impact**: high
  9777	
  9778	### Finding 2: A doctor-style summary should ship beside review
  9779	- **Source**: `external/cmd/modus-memory/doctor.go:13-242`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-crud-health.ts:378-594`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts:236-273`
  9780	- **What it does**: Modus’s `doctor` turns vault health into a one-screen operator report. Public already has deeper health and repair machinery—FTS rebuild, orphan cleanup, degraded/healthy state, confirmation-gated repair—but exposes it as a richer technical envelope.
  9781	- **Why it matters for us**: This is mostly presentation work, not backend work. It improves operator trust immediately while preserving Public’s stronger repair semantics underneath.
  9782	- **Recommendation**: adopt now
  9783	- **Impact**: medium
  9784	
  9785	### Finding 3: Keep one retrieval core; Modus’s split fact-search paths are a warning
  9786	- **Source**: `external/internal/index/indexer.go:287-340`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:290-337`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:273-317`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:771-809`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/search/pipeline/index.ts:1-32`
  9787	- **What it does**: Modus has multiple fact-search contracts for the same memory objects: `Index.SearchFacts`, a separate in-memory `factStore`, and `Vault.SearchFacts` fallback behavior. Public routes `memory_search` through one pipeline contract via `executePipeline`.
  9788	- **Why it matters for us**: This is the strongest architectural lesson from Modus’s weaknesses. Public should keep specialized search surfaces as thin wrappers over the canonical pipeline instead of growing parallel ranking rules that will drift.
  9789	- **Recommendation**: adopt now
  9790	- **Impact**: high
  9791	
  9792	### Finding 4: `memory_due` is real product value, but it needs an authoritative due-state contract first
  9793	- **Source**: `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:273-317,856-897`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:64-157,160-217`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/cognitive/fsrs-scheduler.ts:65-71,177-215`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:519-520`
  9794	- **What it does**: Modus visibly ties search recall, reinforce, decay, and archive to one fact state. Public already stores `stability`, `difficulty`, `last_review`, `review_count`, and opt-in access effects, and computes `nextReviewDate`, but does not expose an operator-facing due queue.
  9795	- **Why it matters for us**: This is the biggest missing workflow surface in Public. But it should not ship until “due” is defined as either persisted state (`next_review_at`) or a deterministic derivation from existing FSRS fields.
  9796	- **Recommendation**: NEW FEATURE
  9797	- **Impact**: high
  9798	
  9799	### Finding 5: Durable proposal inboxes are the best non-retrieval idea Modus has
  9800	- **Source**: `external/internal/vault/prs.go:10-118`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:681-777`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/save/reconsolidation-bridge.ts:417-452`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/checkpoints.ts:681-790`
  9801	- **What it does**: Modus persists risky knowledge changes as markdown PR artifacts, then merge/reject outcomes reinforce or weaken linked beliefs. Public already produces advisory reconsolidation recommendations and confidence feedback, but the recommendation is transient and not stored as a durable review object.
  9802	- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s next gap is operator workflow, not mutation safety. A persistent inbox for reconsolidation, supersession, promotion, and deprecation proposals would let existing confidence and mutation systems work as a real review loop.
  9803	- **Recommendation**: NEW FEATURE
  9804	- **Impact**: high
  9805	
  9806	### Finding 6: Connected-doc hints are worth prototyping only as an explanation appendix
  9807	- **Source**: `external/internal/index/crossref.go:154-214,248-280`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:75-101,901-924`
  9808	- **What it does**: Modus builds lightweight subject/entity/tag adjacency and appends connected docs that did not make the main ranked list. The weighting is simple and fixed (`subject 3`, `entity 2`, `tag 1`).
  9809	- **Why it matters for us**: The transferable part is explanation, not ranking. Public can test a “related memories” appendix without diluting stronger graph-backed or hybrid scoring paths.
  9810	- **Recommendation**: prototype later
  9811	- **Impact**: medium
  9812	
  9813	### Finding 7: Lexical-only expansion belongs only in weak-result recovery
  9814	- **Source**: `external/internal/librarian/search.go:10-52`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:28-58,280-299`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:525-529,771-809`
  9815	- **What it does**: Modus asks the Librarian for 3-5 keyword variants, searches each, deduplicates, and caps results. It is lightweight, but ungrounded and union-first.
  9816	- **Why it matters for us**: Public already has a more complex retrieval pipeline, so copying this as a mainline branch would mostly add noise and latency. The only credible transfer is a tightly bounded fallback when hybrid retrieval is weak.
  9817	- **Recommendation**: prototype later
  9818	- **Impact**: low
  9819	
  9820	### Finding 8: Content-level contradiction and duplicate-fact linting is still worth a prototype
  9821	- **Source**: `external/cmd/modus-memory/doctor.go:42-158`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-crud-health.ts:455-555`
  9822	- **What it does**: Modus’s `doctor` explicitly flags missing `subject`/`predicate`, duplicate `subject+predicate` pairs, and contradictory values for the same pair. Public’s current health surface is stronger on infrastructure integrity than on fact-content linting.
  9823	- **Why it matters for us**: This complements Public’s existing infra health checks instead of replacing them. It is one of the few Modus hygiene ideas that adds net-new value.
  9824	- **Recommendation**: prototype later
  9825	- **Impact**: medium
  9826	
  9827	### Finding 9: Reject Modus’s fuzzy Jaccard result-cache contract
  9828	- **Source**: `external/internal/index/cache.go:10-17,41-119`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:502-529,718-755`
  9829	- **What it does**: Modus reuses cached result sets on exact hash hits or Jaccard-similar query term sets. Public’s search surface has too many scoring knobs—scope, archived filtering, session/causal boost, rerank, quality thresholds, trace/profile flags—for fuzzy query reuse to be safe.
  9830	- **Why it matters for us**: This is the wrong cache contract for Public. Similar text is not enough to guarantee equivalent retrieval intent or scoring context.
  9831	- **Recommendation**: reject
  9832	- **Impact**: high
  9833	
  9834	### Finding 10: Reject Modus’s permissive markdown parse/write contract
  9835	- **Source**: `external/internal/markdown/parser.go:98-159,161-186`; `external/internal/markdown/writer.go:10-52`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts:220-220`
  9836	- **What it does**: Modus treats malformed YAML as body, skips parse failures during scans, and writes markdown directly with minimal validation. That is good for a personal vault, but it optimizes for permissiveness over authoritative ingestion.
  9837	- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s memory layer is intentionally more governed. Regressing to Modus’s permissive storage contract would weaken memory integrity for little gain.
  9838	- **Recommendation**: reject
  9839	- **Impact**: high
  9840	
  9841	### Finding 11: Reject default write-on-read as Public’s default policy
  9842	- **Source**: `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:311-317`; `external/internal/vault/facts.go:188-217`; `.opencode/skill/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts:519-520,797-802`
  9843	- **What it does**: Modus treats every returned fact as a successful recall and asynchronously reinforces it. Public already supports access effects, but keeps them explicit with `trackAccess=false` by default.
  9844	- **Why it matters for us**: Public’s graded FSRS model is stronger than Modus’s success-only reinforce loop. Default write-on-read would blur retrieval and review, inflate successful-recall history, and make future due-state less trustworthy.
  9845	- **Recommendation**: reject
  9846	- **Impact**: high
  9847	
  9848	### Finding 12: Reject trust-stage metadata unless it becomes real gating
  9849	- **Source**: `external/internal/vault/trust.go:11-82`; `external/internal/mcp/vault.go:610-635,681-777`; repo search on `external/internal/**/*.go` shows trust-stage calls only in trust read/write surfaces
  9850	- **What it does**: Modus persists trust stage and exposes get/set tools, but current code does not use that state to gate PR or other mutation tools. It is posture metadata, not enforced runtime policy.
  9851	- **Why it matters for us**: Public should not copy symbolic governance. If autonomy stages are added, they must actually gate review, proposal, or mutation flows.
  9852	- **Recommendation**: reject
  9853	- **Impact**: medium
  9854
